title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. We present HoloGene, an anisotropic conditional INR framework for estimating continuous 3D gene-expression fields from pre-registered ST sections. Its central contribution is an acquisition-aware factorization that couples dense in-plane synthesis with sparse axial evolution using established GAE, FiLM, pseudo-label supervision, and CORAL components. HoloGene compresses high-dimensional expression profiles into a graph-autoencoder latent manifold, uses pseudo-label-derived signature conditioning to provide coarse intra-section context, and applies depth-dependent FiLM modulation to model axial variation. A signature-stratified correlation-alignment regularizer encourages cross-slice covariance alignment in latent features. Using held-out measured sections as cross-sectional references, HoloGene improves reconstruction accuracy and biological preservation metrics compared with general-purpose INRs and adapted spatial-transcriptomics baselines. These results support anisotropic conditional modeling as a practical strategy for estimating 3D expression fields from discontinuous ST sections. Code is available at https://github.com/Szym29/HoloGene.

title: ST-FateFlow: Continuous Gene-Spatial Reconstruction with Differentiation-Potential Learning from Time-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: Time-resolved spatial transcriptomics provides a powerful view of dynamic biological processes by measuring cellular states together with their spatial organization across time. However, destructive profiling and experimental cost restrict observations to a few discrete time points collected from independent samples, with no known cell pairing across time. This makes it difficult to reconstruct gene expression and tissue organization at unobserved stages and to characterize differentiation-associated dynamics. Here, we introduce ST-FateFlow, a flow-matching framework for continuous gene-spatial dynamics and differentiation-potential learning. ST-FateFlow jointly learns gene-expression and spatial-coordinate velocity fields, enabling interpolation of missing time points and continuous modeling of transcriptional evolution and tissue remodeling. In parallel, it independently learns a time-conditioned differentiation potential, whose values organize cell states along inferred differentiation progressions and support the analysis of differentiation-associated transcriptional changes. Across multiple time-resolved spatial transcriptomics datasets, ST-FateFlow effectively captures coordinated gene-expression and spatial dynamics. Case studies further show that the learned potential landscapes are consistent with known developmental and regenerative trajectories and help identify candidate genes associated with differentiation progression.

title: MitoWorld: A Stochastic World Model of the Single-Cell Cycle under Genetic Perturbation
abstract: A cell observed after a gene knockdown has an uncertain future, both in how its appearance will evolve and when it will divide. Existing approaches predict endpoints or population-level changes without jointly modeling individual trajectories and division timing. In this work, we present MitoWorld, a stochastic world model that generates these future appearances as continuous evolution in a Gaussian reference latent, terminated by a division hazard and converted into images by a conditional diffusion renderer. The ordinary transition provably preserves its Gaussian reference, tying its noise to its dynamics; paired observations identify its discrete transition where stationary marginals cannot. The hazard turns division timing into a survival likelihood that can be tested against real cycle lengths. On 325 held-out MitoCheck tracks spanning 17 knockdowns and a control, MitoWorld lowers FID by 34.6\% and the video metric JEDi by 45.6\% relative to the strongest baselines. Its latent-space prediction intervals achieve near-nominal 90\% coverage, are 35\% narrower than those of a model with freely fitted noise. The hazard also yields cell-cycle length distributions with KS distance close to the model-based finite-sample reference. Testable single-cell stochastic dynamics thus offer a generative tool for time-lapse perturbation screens.

title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schrödinger Bridges
abstract: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Cellular dynamics are inherently stochastic and involve changes in population size through proliferation and apoptosis. Growth-based methods represent population change as a rate on the density, which does not assign exits and entries to individual cells. Unbalanced Schrödinger bridges model individual events, but neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training. We introduce Elysium, a simulation-free solver that jointly learns state transition and mass change. Using a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal, Elysium constructs direct regression objectives from an optimal endpoint coupling and conditional bridge distributions, without simulating trajectories during training. We show that the minimizers of the expected training objectives recover the optimal unbalanced Schrödinger bridge. Empirically, Elysium reconstructs state transitions, population size, and event distributions on simulated benchmarks with known killed-diffusion ground truth, outperforming existing deterministic and bridge-based solvers. On single-cell time courses, it interpolates cell state distributions at unobserved time points, tracks population expansion and contraction, and captures biphasic drug-response dynamics.

title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
abstract: Learning the spatiotemporal dynamics of cells from spatial transcriptomics requires connecting snapshots of different cells acquired in different coordinate frames. A rotation or translation of a section can appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence. We introduce horizontal flow matching, which learns changes in tissue organization, molecular state, and cell abundance up to shared rigid motion. The dynamics follow a continuity--reaction equation whose action assigns no cost to shared rigid motion, and the resulting horizontal projector removes this component from spatial prediction errors during learning and from predicted velocities during generation. An equivalent endpoint problem jointly estimates correspondence and relative pose in Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao geometry and yields analytic paths whose velocity and growth serve as regression targets. Regressing these targets recovers the horizontal dynamics under ideal population conditions. Our model, HORIZON, uses an equivariant transformer to predict velocity and growth from the current tissue, so that a tissue can be generated continuously from a single initial snapshot. On a simulated tissue observed in perturbed coordinate frames, alignment improves reconstruction and projection reduces rigid drift. On four spatial transcriptomics time courses, HORIZON reconstructs tissue geometry, gene expression, and cell abundance more accurately than existing spatial and unbalanced trajectory methods, and interpolates held-out developmental stages.

title: GABIF: An Adaptive Guided Graph Denoising Framework for Antibody Conditional Inverse Folding
abstract: Antibodies play a central role in the human immune system, and their design is critical for vaccine development, therapeutic intervention, and improving human longevity. However, the vast combinatorial search space of antibodies poses a fundamental challenge for de novo discovery. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly denoising diffusion models, have demonstrated strong potential in protein inverse folding. Nevertheless, existing approaches are largely constrained to learning from natural antibody repertoires, thereby generating sequences that closely resemble natural antibodies. Such similarity, however, does not necessarily translate into improved functional performance in downstream applications. In this work, we develop a novel generative protein design model that enables the generation and optimization of antibody sequences tailored to specific downstream tasks and target metrics. Besides training on given an antibody dataset, we guide the generative model by an antibody-antigen binding affinity predictor for conditional discrete diffusion. The model is pre-trained on a given antibody dataset. Meanwhile, an antibody-antigen binding affinity predictor is incorporated as a conditional signal in a discrete diffusion framework, where a regressor serves as the conditional probability to guide the learning of the amino acid probability distribution of sequences under the objective of affinity optimization. In silico experiments demonstrate that our antibody design model achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art approaches, while the proposed regressor effectively improves binding affinity, as validated by an independent external predictor. Furthermore, our results highlight that the combination of finetuning and supervised guidance provides a powerful paradigm for adapting pretrained models to downstream tasks.

title: LeCellModel: Interpretable Density Estimation over the Gene Expression Manifold
abstract: Representation learning for single-cell RNA-seq has been evaluated by the identities representations capture -- cell types, lineages, perturbations -- rather than how faithfully they model the distribution of cell states on the gene expression manifold. As a result, density estimation, rare-state detection, perturbation scoring, and gene-level attribution are bolted onto frozen embeddings as separate models, disconnected from the geometry of the data. We argue that modeling the distribution of cell states should be the primary objective, and that representation quality follows from it. Building on LeJEPA, whose SIGReg objective enforces a provably optimal isotropic Gaussian latent, we introduce LeCellModel, which reads the encoder's Jacobian log-volume (JEPA-SCORE) under this Gaussian latent as a relative typicality score. Across several datasets, LeCellModel outperforms established methods on the scIB benchmark for representation quality. Furthermore, we show that LeCellModel enables detection of rare expression states using JEPA-SCORE as a typicality measure, applying it to a controlled cytokine panel, where it identifies stimulated cells across minority fractions and tracks pathway-response magnitude. We introduce gene-level interpretability of the typicality score -- to our knowledge, the first method for analyzing JEPA-SCORE in feature space. Leveraging this framework, LeCellModel recapitulates the known association of a profibrotic macrophage program with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and discovers a CD177+ activated regulatory T cell subpopulation previously described only in tumor contexts. Both findings emerge directly from the geometry of the learned embedding, without relying on supervised annotations.

title: How Far Can Linear Go? BiPert, a Unified Framework for Single-Cell Perturbation Modelling
abstract: Understanding how genetic perturbations affect cellular behaviour is essential for studying gene function and regulatory mechanisms. Large-scale CRISPR screens measure these effects across thousands of genes, but cover relatively few cellular contexts. Predicting perturbation responses in unseen cell types and identifying perturbed genes from their transcriptional effects therefore remain challenging. Here, we show that both tasks can be addressed through a common linear decomposition of transcriptional responses into shared and perturbation-specific components. Building on this principle, we introduce BiPert, a simple linear framework for both forward perturbation prediction and inverse identification. For forward prediction, BiPert outperforms existing methods that use no external biological knowledge when predicting gene expression changes in unseen cell lines. Its few-shot extension, BiPert-FS, adapts to new cell lines using as few as ten measured perturbations. For inverse identification, BiPert-ID identifies perturbed genes from single-cell expression profiles, outperforming deep-learning methods in unseen cell lines and donors. We further show that perturbations whose effects transfer more consistently across cellular contexts are also easier to identify, even after controlling for perturbation effect size. Together, these results establish a connection between perturbation transfer and identification, and demonstrate that simple linear models provide strong, interpretable baselines for both tasks.

title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
abstract: Multimodal protein language models unify sequence and discrete structural tokens via iterative masked decoding, offering a promising paradigm for joint protein design. However, standard decoders rely on a memoryless mask reset at each iteration: only a sparse subset of newly committed hard tokens is carried forward, while all remaining unresolved sites are reset to an identical [MASK] embedding. In open-ended co-generation where neither modality provides a fixed external anchor, this stateless transition limits single-step refinement depth and deprives both tracks of stable cross-step soft anchors, leading to slow convergence or degenerative repetitive collapse. Observing that uncommitted predictions evolve with pronounced temporal coherence rather than erratic noise, we introduce Predictive Memory (PredMem), a training-free self-conditioning recurrence that carries these soft beliefs across steps. At each step, PredMem summarizes raw logits into a probability-weighted Top-$k$ expectation embedding at every residue and affinely interpolates it into eligible masked inputs on the next step at zero extra denoiser cost. Across DPLM-2, DPLM-2.1, and ESM3, PredMem raises unconditional sequence-structure co-generation success by 3.6, 17.7, and 48.7 percentage points, respectively, while improving the quality-diversity trade-off and suppressing repetitive mode collapse. Controlled diagnostics show that these gains stem primarily from early trajectory stabilization in unanchored cross-modal co-evolution rather than extra compute or simple entropy reduction, establishing PredMem as an efficient inference mechanism for multimodal discrete generation.

title: Optimal Transport Meets t-SNE: Integrated Visualization without Batch Effects in OT-tSNE
abstract: Visual exploration is an integral step in understanding the structure of datasets. However, systematic variation between datasets collected under different conditions, known as batch effects, can obscure shared structure and complicate their joint visualization. Existing methods often rely on cross-batch nearest-neighbor relations to integrate the batches. Yet, these local correspondences can be unreliable for challenging cross-batch geometries. We propose optimal-transport t-SNE (OT-tSNE), which replaces nearest-neighbor-based matching with globally coupled affinities derived from entropic optimal transport. Controlled synthetic experiments demonstrated that nearest-neighbor-based methods can deteriorate, while optimal-transport affinities and OT-tSNE embeddings remain robust. Across seven real single-cell datasets, we benchmarked OT-tSNE against a broad range of integration and visualization methods and found that it achieves a Pareto-efficient trade-off between batch mixing and biological conservation, and integrates batches particularly well.

llm.novelty_zh: 用熵正则最优传输得到的全局耦合亲和度替代 t-SNE 中基于最近邻的跨批次匹配，使批次整合式可视化在复杂跨批次几何下更稳健。
llm.summary_zh: 该文提出 OT-tSNE，用熵最优传输的全局耦合亲和度取代基于最近邻的跨批次匹配，以缓解批次效应对联合可视化的干扰。合成实验显示最近邻方法在困难几何下会退化，而 OT 亲和度更稳健；在七个真实单细胞数据集上，该方法在批次混合与生物学保守之间取得帕累托较优的权衡。该工作属于单细胞数据可视化与批次整合，与虚拟细胞建模只有间接关系。

title: Bayesian Learning of Spatially Heterogeneous Causal Structure in Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics preserves the location of each expression profile, making it possible to study how gene regulatory networks differ within a tissue. Across regions of a tissue, regulatory relationships may vary and even reverse direction, so identifying the causal relationships in a specific pathological region can provide insight into therapeutic targets. We propose SpaDAG, a Bayesian method for learning spatially varying causal directed acyclic graphs. By defining the graphs on a triangulation of the tissue, SpaDAG allows each edge to have its own spatial pattern and even to reverse direction across regions. We show that the graphs nonetheless remain fully identifiable, and develop an MCMC sampler that explores them efficiently by reversing an edge over an entire connected region in a single move. SpaDAG outperforms competing methods in simulations with and without direction reversals. In a section spanning a renal cell carcinoma and the adjacent kidney, SpaDAG finds largely different relationships in the two tissues, with those in the tumor concentrated on genes associated with therapeutic targets. Between two of these genes, it identifies a relationship whose direction reverses across the tumor boundary, generating hypotheses about their region-specific coupling. Supplementary materials and code for this article are available online.

datasets_used: renal cell carcinoma and adjacent kidney spatial transcriptomics section (dataset name not given in abstract)

title: Resolving cell states in spatial transcriptomics with SCATTER
abstract: A capture spot can contain transcripts from multiple cell types. Differences between spots may reflect changes in cell-type proportions, expression within a cell type, or both, making local cell-type expression difficult to infer from mixed counts. We developed SCATTER to estimate cell-type proportions and relative expression profiles for each cell type at each spot from spatial transcriptomic counts, coordinates, and annotated single-cell reference data. SCATTER weights reference cell profiles using local spatial context, then jointly fits the resulting profiles and cell-type proportions to reconstruct spot counts. Cell2location estimates regularize the proportions. After fitting, SCATTER uses learned gene-specific calibration factors and fitted proportions to allocate observed counts among cell types. In five pseudo-spot benchmarks constructed from imaging data, SCATTER achieved higher cross-spot correlations with measured expression for 82.8-99.8% of evaluated gene-cell type pairs in pairwise comparisons with DestVI, PANDA, and STged. In breast cancer Xenium data, it recovered gene expression associated with the tumor neighborhood and regulon scores. In breast cancer Visium data, inferred stromal and macrophage expression showed distinct associations with neighborhood malignant cell proportions. In multiple sclerosis brain tissue, SCATTER recovered lesion-associated glial expression programs. In colorectal cancer Visium HD data, it mapped cell-type-specific programs at the invasive front and ranked candidate ligand-receptor pairs. SCATTER enables analysis of spatial expression variation within cell types from mixed tissue measurements.

datasets_used: multiple sclerosis brain tissue spatial transcriptomics
pseudo-spot benchmarks constructed from imaging data

title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
abstract: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.

llm.novelty_zh: 用空间转录组的细胞身份标记基因作为参考，以无监督稀疏自编码器特征聚类来评估病理基础模型是否捕获细胞身份，无需标签即可给出按细胞类型拆分的生物学评分。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作提出 BioScore 基准，用同一组织的空间转录组作为参考，衡量病理图像编码器对 52 种由标记基因定义的细胞身份的捕获程度。方法通过稀疏自编码器将 patch 嵌入拆分为稀疏特征并聚类，再按每种细胞身份评估特征组与表达模式的对应性；在 8 个病理基础模型和 3 个自然图像模型上，病理模型整体优于自然图像模型，且能区分出三个性能梯队。该工作属于病理基础模型评测，与虚拟细胞主题为外围关联。

title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a public-data benchmark of annotation, in silico perturbation and gene regulatory inference
abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network inference. We benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), four newer FMs, CellOracle, supervised perturbation models and task-matched simple baselines on public data, from Perturb-seq screens of cell lines and primary T cells to a brain organoid screen, the developing mouse cortex and lung cancer biopsies, under an analysis plan fixed before the new results. FMs helped most when labels were transferred across species: Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy from human to mouse lung, above every baseline (at most 0.94), and fine-tuned Geneformer V2 reached macro-F1 0.88 from mouse to human, against at most 0.74. In K562, zero-shot perturbations captured the direction of real responses (up to 76% of perturbations), Geneformer V2 tracked CRISPRa effect sizes with its overexpression protocol (rho = 0.30), and its networks recovered tumour differential expression better than co-expression. Within a species, FM embeddings did not exceed principal components. In silico deletions followed target expression and, across seven screens with replicate-level ground truth, met the predefined criterion in none of 81 tests, although in K562 and RPE1 the measured effects replicated between libraries. In contrast, the gene vectors of seven of eight FMs, including three newer models, added to expression features, predicted which knockdowns have large effects in an independent genome-wide K562 screen (rho between 0.34 and 0.44, against 0.26 with expression alone). We release the benchmark and its checks as the fmaudit package.

datasets_used: Perturb-seq screens of cell lines (K562, RPE1)
llm.novelty_zh: 在预先注册的分析计划下，用公开数据系统评测多种单细胞基础模型在细胞注释、in silico 扰动和基因调控网络推断三项任务上的表现，并发布可复现的 fmaudit 基准与检验工具包。

title: XAMPGen: An Interpretable Super Intelligence Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generative super intelligence (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable super intelligence (XSI). We fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties. Generated candidates were screened with an AMP classifier and filtered based on predicted minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), along with human insights into AMP structure and activity in bacterial membranes. A final set of peptides was selected for synthesis and experimental testing. Biological assays confirmed antimicrobial activity in all generated and tested peptides, while fluorescence and circular dichroism measurements characterized membrane binding and peptide structure. We then applied XSI techniques to interpret the generative model and derive biological insights. Specifically, layer probing was used to identify cornerstone layers that encode functionally critical information. Self-attention analysis within these layers revealed residue-level interdependencies and patterns underlying antimicrobial functions, which we evaluated against well-characterized AMPs from the literature. We further examined associations between amino acid sequence patterns and binding properties in bacterial membrane mimics, relating these observations to biological activities in cell-based assays. These analyses provide insight into the model's decision-making process. This builds confidence that the learned amino acid interdependencies have physico-chemical significance, as applied to AMPs, and may facilitate the discovery of novel AMPs with therapeutic potential. This work demonstrates that interpretable generative language models can support rational AMP discovery.

title: Language-guided domain adaptation improves protein sequence representations for antimicrobial resistance analysis
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens complicates infectious disease management. Protein sequences encode molecular features underlying resistance functions such as antibiotic inactivation and drug efflux, providing a basis for investigating bacterial AMR. Protein language models can extract transferable representations from these sequences. However, general purpose protein language models have limited capacity to represent AMR-associated sequences, while task-specific tools often address individual prediction problems. These limitations highlight the need for protein representations that better capture resistance associated functions and can be reused across complementary tasks, supporting systematic AMR analysis from sequence variation to functional relationships among proteins. We developed BacLLM, a language-guided protein representation framework that integrates annotation derived functional knowledge into protein language model representations for AMR analysis in bacterial pathogens. Through sequence enhancement, semantic enrichment of UniProt annotations, and cross modal contrastive learning, BacLLM transfers LLM encoded annotation priors into the sequence encoder, enabling sequence only inference after training. Compared with baseline models, BacLLM provided more informative representations of resistance associated sequences, achieving a mean F1 score of 0.956 across six AMR benchmarks with logistic regression, 2.7 percentage points above the strongest baseline. It also captured resistance associated mutational signals at single residue resolution and preserved taxonomic relationships not reflected by phenotype based clinical groupings. Moreover, BacLLM recovered resistance associated functional organization within a TolC centered protein association network, prioritizing proteins with low sequence identity to TolC but predicted structural similarity to TolC. Extending the same representation framework to an intervention oriented application, BacLLM also improved strain level phage host matching for phage therapy candidate prioritization. Together, these findings establish BacLLM as a reusable protein representation framework for analyzing resistance associated sequence variation and functional organization, with applications in AMR surveillance and phage candidate prioritization.

title: LUCID: joint cell typing and neighbour-aware decontamination of segmented spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Cell profiles in segmented spatial transcriptomics are contaminated by RNA of neighbouring cells and by segmentation errors that merge two cells. LUCID is a multinomial mixture model that jointly assigns a type to each cell, tests whether its profile mixes two types and estimates the fraction of counts coming from its neighbours. An external reference is adapted to the platform, an identifiability rule protects a cell's own signal and the test is calibrated by parametric bootstrap. LUCID works with or without a reference, runs on CPUs and returns integer counts for all genes. On three public Visium HD datasets (mouse brain, human colorectal cancer, mouse liver) and in simulations built on them, LUCID removed contamination from other cell types as well as two-step pipelines, including RCTD followed by DecontX, flagged fewer contaminated cells as mixed, emptied no cell and preserved minority lineages where one cell type dominates.

llm.novelty_zh: 将细胞类型指派、两类型混合检验与邻近细胞污染比例估计联合在一个多项混合模型中，并用参数化自助法校准，同时修正分割错误造成的合并细胞。
llm.summary_zh: LUCID 是一个多项混合模型，用于分割后的空间转录组数据：它同时为每个细胞分配类型、检验其表达谱是否混合了两种类型，并估计来自邻近细胞的 counts 比例。在三个公开的 Visium HD 数据集（小鼠脑、人结直肠癌、小鼠肝）及其模拟数据上，它比 RCTD 加 DecontX 的两步流程更好地去除其他细胞类型的污染，标记为混合的污染细胞更少，且不会清空任何细胞。该工作属于空间组学数据预处理与细胞类型注释，与虚拟细胞建模的关联较间接。

title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
abstract: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence. Non recurrent patients showed enrichment of immune related processes, whereas recurrent cases were characterized by pathways associated with invasion and metastasis. Notably, a loss of interaction in the HSPG pathway between CALB1+ and stromal cells was observed in recurrent patients, suggesting a potential disruption of cell matrix adhesion mechanisms. To verify the reliability of this finding, we applied the framework to spatial transcriptomics data, which confirmed the presence of the HSPG2 DAG1 interaction in non-recurrent tumors and its near absence in recurrent ones. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

title: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell
abstract: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. Existing methods for identifying spatially organized cell populations rely on cellular niches defined by neighboring cells, leaving open whether such populations can be identified from individual-cell representations alone. Moreover, representations that jointly capture transcript identity and three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization have not been systematically learned or biologically evaluated. Here we present a representation learning framework that models each cell as a gene-annotated point cloud of transcripts and trains a rotation-equivariant neural network to reconstruct 3D cell shape, yielding spatially informed transcript embeddings. We further aggregate these embeddings into a cell-state representation that summarizes transcript-level spatial patterns. Our framework outperforms existing point-cloud-based 3D reconstruction methods on cell-shape reconstruction. In MERFISH human uterine cancer, combining the learned embeddings with gene expression improved prediction of CD45RO protein intensity over both gene expression alone and niche-based embeddings. Applied to MERFISH human liver cancer and Xenium human lung datasets, our framework identified distinct spatial patterns between cell populations, including spatially organized subpopulations marked by disease-associated gene expression and patterns associated with pathological tissue structures. Together, these results show that learning transcript representations through 3D cell reconstruction provides a novel approach to capture cell-state heterogeneity and biologically relevant spatial organization in subcellular spatial transcriptomics.

title: Pallatom2: Navigating the De Novo Protein Universe with Atom-to-Atom Modeling
abstract: Protein binder design requires precise coordination of molecular structure, binding geometry, and experimentally measurable performance. We introduce Pallatom2, an efficient, precise Atom-to-Atom generative model that jointly models protein sequence, backbone conformation, side-chain geometry, and target-interface contacts. A unified Atom14 representation and residue-guided sparse all-atom attention enable bidirectional information exchange between residue-level and atom-level representations, coordinating global structure with local atomic detail in a compact model of just 65.9 million parameters. Its conditioning system provides fine-grained control over binder-target engagement and global and local protein conformations, supporting diverse target-specific design requirements. In silico evaluation demonstrates broad generative capability across long-chain monomers, multi-domain proteins, and homomultimers, with monomer sampling extending to 1,600 residues. In binder design, Pallatom2 achieves state-of-the-art in silico screening performance across all nine targets with cross-method benchmark data under the reported protocols. These in silico results translate into substantial experimental success: biolayer interferometry identifies 112 active designs among 210 tested candidates (53.3%), with binders obtained for all ten experimentally evaluated targets. Six targets yield picomolar-scale apparent affinities, including K_D values of 3.96 pM for SC2RBD and 33.8 pM for PD-L1, while TNF reaches 1.166 nM. Beyond de novo discovery, starting-interface-guided BCMA design preserves association kinetics despite substantial sequence divergence; partial diffusion improves TNF affinity by up to 7.57-fold; and CDR-associated interface remodeling converts an inactive de novo nanobody into binders with apparent K_D values of 4.31 and 5.93 nM. Together, these results establish Pallatom2 as a versatile model for protein design, combining efficient atomic modeling, leading in silico screening performance, and experimentally demonstrated capabilities in high-affinity binder discovery, interface transfer, affinity maturation, and recovery of inactive designs.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 65.9M 参数的原子级（Atom14）蛋白生成模型，用残基引导的稀疏全原子注意力联合建模序列、骨架、侧链与靶点界面，并通过 210 个候选中 112 个活性设计的湿实验验证了 pM 级结合物。
llm.summary_zh: Pallatom2 是一个面向蛋白结合物设计的原子到原子生成模型，联合建模序列、主链构象、侧链几何与靶点界面接触，并支持界面迁移、亲和力成熟等条件控制。计算评估显示其在九个靶点上取得领先的 in silico 筛选表现，湿实验中 210 个候选有 112 个具有活性，多个靶点达到皮摩尔级亲和力。该工作属于蛋白设计范畴，与虚拟细胞主线为外围关系。

title: Scalable Multi-omics Diagonal Integration from Self-Mapping
abstract: Diagonal integration seeks to align single-cell multi-omics datasets in which distinct modalities, such as RNA and protein, are measured in different cells. Unlike horizontal integration, these datasets lack direct cell--cell correspondences and complete feature mappings across modalities. Leading methods for weak-linkage integration often infer anchor cells between modalities by searching for cross-modal similarities through predefined feature links, then use these anchors to guide alignment. Their required matching or anchor refinement can become computationally burdensome at atlas scale. Here, we introduce a novel self-mapping technique, a mechanism that aligns modalities by mapping each computationally decoded cross-modality omics profile prediction to its own observed inputs. We implement this strategy in SCALEMAP, a scalable, modality-agnostic method for diagonal integration. Across transcriptomic, epigenomic and proteomic benchmarks, SCALEMAP matches or outperforms leading alternatives while requiring substantially less runtime and memory. In large-scale experiments, SCALEMAP integrates more than 1.5 million multi-omic profiles in less than 5 minutes with under 20 GB peak memory, which enables rapid synthesis of massive single-cell multi-omics resources into unified biological representations.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 self-mapping 机制用于单细胞跨模态（diagonal）整合，强调可扩展性（150 万细胞 5 分钟内完成）。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作针对单细胞多组学对角整合（不同模态在不同细胞中测量、无细胞对应关系）的问题，提出 self-mapping 技术，将每个跨模态预测映射回其自身观测输入以实现对齐，并实现为 SCALEMAP。方法在转录组、表观组和蛋白组基准上与主流方法相当或更优，同时显著降低运行时间和内存。它主要面向大规模单细胞多组学数据的快速统一表征，与虚拟细胞的扰动建模或细胞基础模型关系较弱。

title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints. The detected instances are then used by a set of regressors trained under a multiple-instance, multiple-target regression setting to predict precise single-cell gene expression counts. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic and Visium-like datasets demonstrate that st2sc significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accurately segmenting cellular instances and predicting gene counts. The method can further resolve contested 2um bin in Visium HD. Application to human IPF lung showed the model can recover the subtype marker level analysis. This advancement further improves single-cell resolution analysis in spatial transcriptomics, facilitating more accurate downstream biological analyses.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 AGFT 算法，从 Vision-Gene Transformer 的注意力梯度流中识别细胞实例，并结合多实例多目标回归，从多细胞空间转录组数据推断单细胞基因表达。
llm.summary_zh: 本文提出 st2sc 框架，用于从 Visium 等多细胞空间转录组数据中推断单细胞基因表达谱，包括细胞实例分割和逐基因表达计数预测两步。方法基于 Attention Gradient Flow Tracking 从 Vision-Gene Transformer 提取注意力图来检测候选细胞，并用多实例多目标回归器预测单细胞计数。作者在合成数据、Visium-like 数据、Visium HD 的 2um bin 及人类 IPF 肺组织上进行了评估。该工作属于空间组学超分辨率/单细胞分解方向，与虚拟细胞主题仅有间接关联。

title: Revealing the transcriptomic organization of extrasomatic interfaces using SCOUBI
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) generates substantial transcript signal outside segmented cell bodies, which is generally discarded by analysis tools. This is especially problematic for brain ST data, as neuronal mRNAs can be localized far from somata - in axons, dendrites, and synaptic compartments - and up to half of the transcripts in ST data may lie outside cell bodies. Here, we present SCOUBI, a computational framework that identifies axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in ST data, revealing a hitherto overlooked layer of molecular function in neural tissues. It first partitions extrasomatic space into axon- and dendrite-enriched compartments based on known marker genes, using a neural network trained to maximize marker specificity and inter-compartment communication signals. It then defines interfaces as loci where predicted axonal and dendritic compartments converge and exhibit ligand-receptor colocalization. Applied to mouse brain, SCOUBI creates maps of axonal and dendritic compartments and their interfaces that align with known spatial patterns of neurite and synaptic distribution. It identifies transcriptomic differences between interfaces and the surrounding extrasomatic space, revealing region-specific signatures of neuronal signaling and synaptic plasticity. By comparing interface transcript enrichment with local somatic expression, SCOUBI identifies genes that preferentially localize at sites of intercellular communication rather than simply reflecting nearby cell bodies. SCOUBI reveals interface-associated transcripts beyond established synaptic genes, with molecular signatures reproducible across independent samples and imaging platforms. In summary, SCOUBI transforms a substantial and often-discarded aspect of ST data into an interpretable readout of subcellular organization and neural signaling.

llm.novelty_zh: 首次系统地利用空间转录组中细胞体外（extrasomatic）的RNA信号，通过神经网络划分轴突/树突区室并识别二者交汇处的轴突-树突界面及配体-受体共定位，揭示突触相关的亚细胞转录组结构。
llm.summary_zh: SCOUBI 是一个针对空间转录组数据中细胞体外（extrasomatic）RNA 的计算框架，利用已知标记基因和神经网络将胞外空间划分为轴突与树突富集区室，并识别二者汇聚处的轴突-树突界面。应用于小鼠脑组织，它揭示了区域特异的神经信号与突触可塑性相关转录特征，并能区分在细胞间通讯位点富集、而非仅由邻近胞体决定的基因。该工作聚焦于空间转录组的亚细胞解析分析，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型的主题关联较弱。

title: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types
abstract: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation. To capture these complementary sources of information in the CNS, we introduce SEMPER, a multimodal representation learning model that aligns protein language model representations with protein-protein interaction networks from 442 cell types of the adult human brain, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which its gene is expressed. We show that SEMPER representations predict cell type-specific protein complexes and predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen. In zero-shot retrieval, SEMPER recovers clinically pursued drug targets for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at higher rates than cell type-specific models. To further improve target recovery, we combine SEMPER with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations. The combination recovers more targets, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

title: Reproducibility and cross-dataset concordance of drug-induced transcriptional responses
abstract: Drug-perturbation transcriptomic resources are expanding, but the reproducibility and cross-source consistency of the responses they measure remain critical to their use. We compared six resources using independent replicates, matched-drug analyses, and response decomposition. High agreement in treated expression did not translate into equally repeatable drug-induced changes. Cross-source response concordance was generally limited, including under matched cell and treatment conditions, although some comparisons retained drug-specific information. In Tahoe, a control-expression-only baseline left substantial drug-specific variation unresolved. Measured drug main effects - the average responses across cell lines - provided information for predicting cell-specific interactions, with this relationship retained in a cross-plate validation. Exploratory analyses of structure, target, and external-response representations identified modest signals in selected pipelines. Together, these analyses characterize the reliability and transferability of current perturbation resources and identify prediction of drug main effects as a key bottleneck in the framework examined, motivating shared reference measurements and better recovery of drug-specific responses.

llm.novelty_zh: 首次系统比较六个药物扰动转录组资源的可重复性与跨来源一致性，并将药物主效应（跨细胞系平均响应）识别为预测细胞特异性药物相互作用的关键瓶颈。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究利用独立重复、匹配药物分析和响应分解，评估了六个药物扰动转录组资源的可重复性与跨来源一致性，发现处理后表达的高一致性并不等同于药物诱导变化的可重复性。研究显示测得的药物主效应可为预测细胞特异性相互作用提供信息，并在跨板验证中保持该关系，从而指出药物主效应预测是当前框架中的主要瓶颈。

title: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
abstract: Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge. At inference, DynamicsPLM computes zero-shot mutation effects from sequence alone by balancing an evolutionary plausibility score against a structural dynamics disruption score. Across the massive ProteinGym benchmark and natural variants of the Tsuboyama folding stability dataset, DynamicsPLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among all models under 100M parameters, and matches or outperforms several billion-scale sequence-based models of its size. Our findings demonstrate that explicit structural-dynamics supervision provides a parameter-efficient alternative to raw scale. Availability: All codes including data preparation scripts, training and validation recipes, and experimental configurations for LoMuS are available at: https://github.com/kabir-ai2bio-lab/DynamicsPLM.

llm.novelty_zh: 在小参数量（35M）蛋白语言模型上，通过二阶段多任务持续预训练把残基级和成对分子动力学头注入进序列编码器，并用进化合理性与结构动力学破坏分数相结合做零样本突变效应预测。
llm.summary_zh: 论文提出 DynamicsPLM，一个 35M 参数的蛋白语言模型，通过在约 6 万条蛋白上做多任务持续预训练，把分子动力学监督融入序列编码器。模型在 ProteinGym 和 Tsuboyama 稳定性数据上报告了百兆参数以下的最优结果，并与部分十亿级序列模型相当或更好。该工作属于蛋白变异效应预测，与虚拟细胞主线只有间接关系，故归为外围圈。

title: Phylospatial optimal transport for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data integration
abstract: The spatial organization of evolving cell populations in tumors influences how they progress and respond to treatment. Spatially resolved transcriptomics data may be used to examine the locations of these diverse cell states in tumor sections. However, these technologies often lack single-cell resolution and instead capture groups of cells in spatial spots, making it difficult to resolve cancer clones. In contrast, dissociated single-cell transcriptomics data are better suited for obtaining cell lineages, but do not capture the locations of the cells in the tissue. Here, we introduce SpOTr, an optimal transport approach that leverages the concordance between the evolutionary tree and the spatial distribution of cancer cells to integrate single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data from tumors. SpOTr combines a spot deconvolution model with Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport, in which cells that are close in the tree are drawn to nearby spots. In simulations and in real spatial lineage tracing data, SpOTr recovered the spatial locations of clones better than methods that ignore the tree. In a human colorectal liver metastasis, SpOTr mapped copy number clones from dissociated cells to spatial spots, showing that it successfully maps the evolutionary history of tumors in space.

llm.novelty_zh: 将进化树（克隆谱系）作为先验，用 Fused Gromov-Wasserstein 最优传输结合 spot 解卷积，把单细胞克隆映射到空间 spot。
llm.summary_zh: SpOTr 是一种最优传输方法，利用肿瘤细胞进化树与空间分布的一致性，将解离单细胞转录组与空间转录组数据整合。方法结合 spot 解卷积模型与 Fused Gromov-Wasserstein 最优传输，使进化树上相近的细胞被拉向空间上相近的 spot。模拟与真实空间谱系追踪数据表明其克隆空间定位优于忽略进化树的方法。该工作聚焦肿瘤克隆的空间作图，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型关系较弱。

title: Single-cell transfer RNA sequencing reveals principles of translational regulation
abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) decode genetic instructions from messenger RNA (mRNA) into protein, yet their abundance and regulation across cell states remain largely undefined, as multimodal measures of cellular tRNAs have remained elusive. Here, we develop a massively parallel assay for single-cell translatome and RNA sequencing (sctRNA-seq), which profiles transcriptome-wide mRNA and tRNA abundance simultaneously and chart the tRNA composition of 364,841 cells. Through multimodal perturbation screening of protein-coding genes and tRNA loci, we reveal dynamics across the mRNA and tRNA transcriptomes, delineating distinct tRNA-linked modules regulated by metabolic and Pol III-mediated transcription. Further, we uncover a close correspondence between codon demand and tRNA-mediated anticodon composition during hematopoietic multilineage commitment and differentiation. Tri-modal profiling of mRNA, tRNA, and proteins from primary human T cells reveals tRNA-mediated regulation that partially explains the discordance between mRNA and protein levels, particularly for selenoproteins and transcription factors. Finally, we uncover a stress-responsive tRNA module defined by gene-internal promoter sequences. Together, our analyses resolve tRNAs as a previously undefined layer of translational control underlying cellular identity and cell-state transitions.
affiliations: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, NY

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 sctRNA-seq 单细胞 tRNA 与 mRNA 同步测序方法，并结合多模态扰动筛选与 mRNA-tRNA-蛋白三模态分析，将 tRNA 确立为翻译调控层。
llm.summary_zh: 该文开发了可同时检测转录组范围 mRNA 与 tRNA 丰度的单细胞翻译组测序方法 sctRNA-seq，并在 364,841 个细胞中刻画了 tRNA 组成。通过对蛋白编码基因和 tRNA 位点的多模态扰动筛选，作者揭示了 tRNA 模块受代谢与 Pol III 转录调控，并在造血分化中发现密码子需求与反密码子组成的对应关系。三模态（mRNA、tRNA、蛋白）数据进一步表明 tRNA 调控可部分解释 mRNA 与蛋白水平的不一致。

title: Chimera: Cross-Species Single-Cell Generative Modeling of Expression Deployment Relative to Protein Conservation
abstract: A protein's sequence says what a gene could do in another species; the cells of that species say what it does there. Comparative genomics measures the first. Chimera measures the second, a gene's deployment, on the same genes and reports the difference. It aligns single-cell atlases across species in one generative model and returns, for every one-to-one ortholog, the evidence in the counts for a shared expression pattern, and {Delta}[a], the position of that evidence above or below what the protein's identity predicts. This difference is not sequence constraint under another name: across eight tissues, protein identity tracks dN/dS, whereas {Delta}[a] tracks neither. A gene therefore has two coordinates, not one, and the second can contradict the first: spermatocyte genes such as ZPBP2 keep their stage pattern on less conserved proteins, in eight held-out species, whereas conserved hepatocyte enzymes such as ALAS1 share their pattern but not their level. More broadly, genes of specialized cells sit above what their proteins predict in 23 of 24 cohorts, and approved drug targets do so more often than matched genes. Even among nearly identical proteins, where sequence can no longer tell genes apart, the count evidence still does. Nor does this rest on the model alone: independent data support the count evidence in liver and testis and, in a pre-specified test, {Delta}[a] in liver. With both coordinates, one can ask whether another species uses a gene as humans do, the premise of every animal model of a disease gene or drug target.

llm.novelty_zh: 提出基因在跨物种中的"表达部署"（Δ[a]）作为独立于蛋白序列保守性的第二维度，通过跨物种单细胞生成模型对同源基因进行量化，并与dN/dS、蛋白同一性相区分。
llm.summary_zh: Chimera 在统一的生成模型中对齐多个物种的单细胞图谱，为每个一对一直系同源基因给出共享表达模式的计数证据，以及相对于蛋白同一性预测值的偏移量 Δ[a]。该指标与蛋白序列保守性（dN/dS）基本独立，在多个组织、队列和留出物种中可区分基因的部署模式，并获得独立数据的部分支持。该工作为判断另一物种是否以与人类相同的方式使用某基因提供了框架。

title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics mapping of human ovarian aging across young and menopausal transition
abstract: Ovarian aging is an early feature of human aging with broad consequences for women's health, yet its cellular dynamics across the menopausal transition remain unclear. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic, chromatin accessibility and spatial transcriptomic profiles across young, menopausal-transition and postmenopausal human ovaries. Granulosa cells (GCs) exhibited the most pronounced age-associated transcriptional remodelling. The menopausal transition was characterized by reduced DNA-repair activity and elevated stress-response programs in GCs, alongside broader changes in hormone-response and steroid-metabolic programs during ovarian aging. Integrated regulatory analyses implicated HEYL, a GC-enriched transcription factor, with reduced accessibility at a putative regulatory element during aging. Genetic analyses associated HEYL and its predicted upstream regulators with age at natural menopause, while spatial mapping revealed enrichment of menopause-associated genetic signals in GC-rich regions. HEYL depletion increased senescence-associated phenotypes in human granulosa-like cells and primary mouse GCs, whereas overexpression attenuated oxidative-stress-induced senescence. Perturbation of its orthologue Hey produced consistent effects in Drosophila ovaries. Together, our atlas reveals stage-associated granulosa-cell remodeling and implicates HEYL in ovarian aging.
affiliations: Department of Gynecology, Women's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, China

llm.novelty_zh: 首次在人类卵巢衰老及绝经过渡期整合单细胞转录组、染色质可及性与空间转录组图谱，并通过 HEYL 敲降/过表达实验在人源细胞、小鼠 GC 与果蝇中验证其对衰老表型的作用。

title: Mapping Senescence Landscapes in Metabolic Liver Disease Progression
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects more than 30% of the population, often progressing from reversible steatosis to irreversible fibrosis and cirrhosis. Although cellular senescence is implicated in driving MASLD, the evidence in human tissue and the mechanism are lacking. Here, we apply spatial transcriptomics and scRNAseq to human liver samples spanning healthy to fibrotic disease to address these knowledge gaps. Using a combination of cell stress, cell cycle arrest, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and inflammatory genes, senescent microenvironments termed "SenSpots" were identified by Visium transcriptomics that predominantly localized to portal tracts and fibrotic septa across all specimens. Functional profiling revealed a fundamental phenotypic divergence: SenSpots in healthy liver displayed a physiological wound-healing and tissue-development program, whereas SenSpots in fibrotic tissue expressed genes related to inflammation, stress, and ECM-disassembly. Spatial deconvolution and network expansion analyses demonstrated that SenSpots act as epicenters for TGF-{beta}, NOTCH, complement, and ECM-reorganization signaling, which spreads into the surrounding tissue microenvironment as disease advances. Furthermore, scRNAseq data validated the Visium results and identified a previously unappreciated population of senescent Schwann cells in the diseased liver niche. These findings map the spatial origination and paracrine propagation of pathological senescence and identify senotypes associated with liver fibrosis.

title: Spindle: Scalable Indexing of Spatial-Omics Data for Fast Querying
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has unlocked new avenues for biological discovery by jointly capturing gene expression and spatial context. ST datasets are typically stored as gene expression matrices paired with spatial coordinates, supporting queries based on expression levels at individual locations. However, characterizing how genes vary together requires representations of relationships between genes, such as covariance matrices computed over spatial neighborhoods. These gene--gene co-expression patterns capture coordinated biological variation and can reveal spatially localized gene programs. As datasets grow to atlas scale, efficiently searching for such patterns becomes a central computational bottleneck due to the combination of high dimensionality, extreme sparsity, and variability in gene expression across large numbers of spatial regions. Such searches require repeated access to second-order statistics, motivating a compact, searchable representation of spatial co-expression. We address this problem with Spindle, a platform-agnostic indexing algorithm for efficiently searching spatial gene co-expression patterns. Spindle exploits the approximate block-diagonal structure of gene--gene covariance matrices over spatial regions, in which covariances between blocks are small in magnitude, to selectively store informative components while compactly representing recurring covariance patterns. This yields a compressed yet searchable index suitable for atlas-scale spatial datasets. Across multiple real-world biological datasets (87,000--817,000 cells), Spindle indexes are 113--197 times smaller than the whole covariance matrices. A complete query, including query preprocessing, takes 2.8--28 ms on one CPU core, 5.1--16 times faster than a scan over the whole covariance matrices, and the tiles it returns recover a median of 81% of the exact near neighbors. In breast cancer, the regions retrieved by covariance search closely match the cell-type composition of the query (median cell-type composition difference 0.15, compared with 0.54 for random regions). Spindle supports both partial covariance queries and queries specified as gene lists, as well as retrieval across measurement platforms.

llm.novelty_zh: 利用空间区域内基因-基因协方差矩阵近似块对角的结构，构建紧凑且可检索的空间共表达索引，用于图谱级空间组学数据的快速查询。

title: Graph-guided flow matching enables biologically informed prediction at single-cell resolution
abstract: Perturb-seq enables systematic interrogation of massively parallel genetic perturbations at single-cell resolution, yet exhaustive characterization of the full perturbation space remains impractical. Here, we present Graph-guided Flow Matching (GFM), a generative framework that integrates biological knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict post-perturbation single-cell transcriptomes. Across multiple large-scale Perturb-seq datasets, GFM outperforms a strong linear baseline and current deep-learning models in predicting unseen single-gene perturbations, while training up to 30x faster and remaining robust with limited training data. GFM also demonstrates competitive performance in the two-gene perturbation prediction task when neither perturbed gene is observed during training. Ablation experiments show that combining flow matching with knowledge graphs enables accurate prediction of perturbation responses. Finally, GFM accurately calculates transcriptional consequences of HSP90AA1 inactivation and identifies target candidates unseen by the model in chronic myeloid leukemia. Our study establishes GFM as a biologically informed generative framework that predicts single-cell perturbation responses for prioritization of therapeutic targets.
affiliations: TRON - Translational Oncology at the University Medical Center of the Johannes Gutenberg University gGmbH, Mainz, Germany

datasets_used: Perturb-seq datasets (multiple large-scale, unnamed in abstract)
