title: HieraPTM: From PTM Site Recognition to Functional Phosphosite Prediction through Hierarchical Context and Protein Mechanics
abstract: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate cellular signaling and protein function, making accurate site identification essential for understanding protein regulation. However, PTM site recognition and functional phosphosite prediction are largely modeled independently, limiting the transfer of large-scale recognition knowledge to functional prioritization. Here, we introduce HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos, a cross-task hierarchical framework that separately models and conditionally integrates transferable PTM recognition representations and function-specific mechanical evidence. HieraPTM integrates local sequence patterns, protein language model representations, and three-dimensional structural information to recognize multiple PTM types. HieraFuncPhos transfers these representations through parameter-efficient adaptation and adaptively retrieves local and distal mechanical evidence conditioned on functional representations. At HSP90AA1 T36 and T115, the model reveals distinct mechanical response patterns consistent with published nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) observations, suggesting that the framework not only prioritizes functional phosphosites but also provides biophysically grounded, testable hypotheses regarding site-specific regulation. HieraPTM achieved macro-averaged AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.9237 and 0.8425 across eight PTM tasks, while maintaining competitive performance on severely imbalanced external benchmarks. HieraFuncPhos achieved an AUROC of 0.8274 and an AUPRC of 0.8188, outperforming existing comparison methods. Together, this framework connects PTM site recognition, functional prioritization, and structure-informed hypotheses regarding potential regulatory processes.

llm.novelty_zh: 将PTM位点识别的层级表征通过参数高效适配迁移到功能磷酸化位点预测，并结合结构力学证据给出特定位点调控假设（如HSP90AA1 T36/T115）。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作提出HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos框架，融合局部序列模式、蛋白语言模型表征与三维结构信息识别多种PTM位点，并通过参数高效适配将其迁移到功能磷酸化位点优先级排序。摘要显示其在八个PTM任务和功能磷酸化位点预测上取得较高AUROC/AUPRC，并与HSP90AA1已发表的NMR观察相符。该工作属于蛋白翻译后修饰预测，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型关系较弱。

title: Spatial multi-omic profiling of non-autonomous transcriptomic and epigenomic responses to genetic perturbation
abstract: Multicellular organisms develop and maintain differentiated cell states through a combination of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, including signal transduction pathways mediated by ligands, receptors, and kinases. Genetic perturbation through CRISPR pooled screening is widely used to study cell-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, but the challenges of cellular-resolution in situ measurement have limited the study of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms. We developed Perturb-Tags, a spatial multi-omic technique for pooled CRISPR screening that tags nuclei with spatial barcodes, allowing joint measurement of single-nucleus gene expression, CRISPR guide RNAs, chromatin accessibility, and spatial positions within intact tissue. Perturb-Tags achieves cellular-resolution, unbiased gene expression and multi-omic profiling, and higher sensitivity than previous spatial perturbation approaches. We used Perturb-Tags to systematically perturb ligands, receptors, and all expressed kinases in human embryoid bodies. These experiments revealed extensive non-autonomous gene expression changes after perturbation, including distance-dependent loss of signaling pathway activity upon ligand knockdown, compensatory upregulation of alternative signaling pathways, and responses to receptor and kinase knockdown that vary with cell microenvironment. We also identified changes in the spatial organization of cells with ligand and kinase knockdowns. Finally, we trained a graph neural network to model the combined effects of genetic perturbations on gene expression and chromatin accessibility across an entire tissue. Our work provides a powerful experimental and computational platform for mechanistic studies of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms across healthy and diseased tissues.

datasets_used: Perturb-Tags spatial CRISPR screen in human embryoid bodies (in-house experimental data)
llm.novelty_zh: 提出 Perturb-Tags 空间多组学 CRISPR pooled screen 技术，在组织原位同时测量单核基因表达、gRNA、染色质可及性与空间位置，并用 GNN 建模整个组织内扰动对基因表达和染色质可及性的联合效应，首次系统揭示配体/受体/激酶扰动的非自主调控响应。
llm.summary_zh: 作者开发了 Perturb-Tags，一种通过空间条形码标记细胞核的空间多组学 pooled CRISPR 筛选方法，用于人类 embryoid body 中对配体、受体及所有表达激酶进行系统扰动。实验揭示了距离依赖的信号通路活性丧失、代偿性旁路激活以及随微环境变化的扰动响应，并观察到细胞空间组织的改变。最后，作者训练图神经网络（GNN）在整个组织范围内建模遗传扰动对基因表达与染色质可及性的联合影响。

title: Integrating Unsupervised Clustering with Transformer-Based Models for De Novo Cell Population Identification
abstract: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing has been widely applied across the life sciences. It enables accurate and robust identification of cell types in heterogeneous biological tissues through unsupervised clustering, shallow learning, and deep learning. While deep learning does not outperform shallow learning in classification performance, it streamlines cell type identification by eliminating cumbersome preprocessing procedures. However, the availability of training datasets with comprehensive cell type annotations is always limited, so new datasets inevitably contain cell populations that are not pre-defined in the training data. To address this limitation, we integrated unsupervised clustering with transformer-based models to identify cell populations unrecognized by classical methods. Specifically, we developed the Nankai GeneRank Classifier by fine-tuning the pre-trained Geneformer-V1 model, and then clustered cells based on its softmax-normalized class probability matrix (SCPM). Applied to a public colorectal cancer dataset, the new method, named SCPM-based clustering, resolved cell populations that cannot be unambiguously identified by classical methods alone and led to the discovery of novel candidate markers of colorectal cancer stem cells, demonstrating its utility.
affiliations: College of Life Sciences, Nankai University, Tianjin

datasets_used: public colorectal cancer scRNA-seq dataset (name not given in abstract)
llm.novelty_zh: 将微调后的 Geneformer-V1 输出的 softmax 归一化类别概率矩阵（SCPM）作为表征进行无监督聚类，用于识别训练集中未预定义的细胞群，并据此在结直肠癌数据中发现候选癌症干细胞标志物。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作针对单细胞注释中训练数据类别不全的问题，提出 Nankai GeneRank Classifier（微调 Geneformer-V1），并对其 softmax 类别概率矩阵 SCPM 进行无监督聚类，以发现经典方法难以明确识别的细胞群。在公开结直肠癌数据集上的应用显示该方法能解析部分细胞群，并提示了若干结直肠癌干细胞的候选标志物。整体属于基于单细胞基础模型的细胞类型识别应用型方法，方法增量和数据验证范围有限。

title: Regional Signals Matter: Rethinking Global Pooling for mRNA Foundation Models
abstract: RNA foundation models with diverse architectures have shown promise for learning representations of messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences. However, existing benchmarks commonly reduce token-level embeddings to transcript-level representations through global mean pooling before fitting a downstream probe. This aggregation does not explicitly preserve the identities of biologically distinct mRNA regions. Consequently, signals associated with short regulatory regions may be diluted, confounding assessments of representation quality with the information preserved by the readout. We introduce an architecture-agnostic, region-aware readout that separately averages embeddings within the 5$'$ untranslated region (UTR), coding sequence, and 3$'$ UTR and concatenates the resulting representations for linear probing. We reproduce mRNABench evaluations for 20 frozen models from 18 families, with a median absolute score difference of 0.0009 across 380 model--dataset--target evaluations published for 19 models, and construct a region-aware benchmark using the same models, tasks, and splits. Relative to global mean pooling, region-aware pooling increases Pearson correlation, averaged across the 20 models, by 11--25\% on translation and stability tasks, with no statistically significant decreases detected for any model on the regression tasks. On classification tasks, relative changes in the area under the precision--recall curve range from $-3\%$ to $+11\%$. Boundary randomization and displacement generally reduce performance, while dimensionality-matched and sequence-composition controls indicate that the gains are not explained solely by increased feature dimensionality, region length, or guanine--cytosine (GC) content. Learned attention pooling approaches region-aware performance only when supplied with one query per region. In silico perturbations reveal stronger sensitivity to upstream AUGs (uAUGs) and their Kozak context, while analyses of endogenous transcripts show approximately threefold greater recovery of length- and GC-adjusted uAUG-associated differences than global-mean probes. Both readouts capture codon optimality. Model rankings averaged over the regression tasks remain largely stable, while within a task models move by several places. Our region-aware benchmark therefore provides a biologically structured and complementary evaluation of mRNA foundation models, revealing regulatory information that is less accessible to linear probes after global mean pooling. The code is available at \url{https://github.com/Sanford-Labs/rnaregionpooling

llm.novelty_zh: 提出与模型架构无关的区域感知（5'UTR、CDS、3'UTR 分区平均）读出方式，替代全局均值池化，并据此构建区域感知的 mRNA 基础模型基准。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作指出 mRNA 基础模型基准中常用的全局均值池化会稀释短调控区域的信号，因此提出按 5'UTR、CDS、3'UTR 分别平均再拼接的区域感知读出方式，用于线性探针。在 20 个冻结模型上复现 mRNABench 并与全局池化对比，翻译和稳定性回归任务的 Pearson 相关性普遍提升，并通过 uAUG 与密码子最优性等分析验证其生物学可解释性。该工作属于 mRNA 表征评测方法学，与虚拟细胞核心问题只有间接关系。

title: ModBERT: a DNA modification and genetic variant-aware DNA large language model
abstract: The development of foundation models that learn a general grammar of DNA (DNA language models) has accelerated in recent years. The vast majority of DNA large language models (LLMs), such as DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, are pretrained almost exclusively on reference genomes. They therefore cannot represent the two sources of variation most directly tied to regulatory differences between people: genetic variants and DNA methylation. Long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) now measures both from the same native DNA molecules, but no model is designed to use this joint readout. With this in mind, we developed ModBERT, a DNA language model built on a five-letter probabilistic genome representation in which each position is a distribution over A, C, G, T, 5mC (represented with M). In pretraining, these distributions encode population allele frequencies and CpG methylation levels from 242 individuals in the 1000 Genomes Long-Read Sequencing Consortium, learned with a soft-target masked language modeling objective. We further propose probabilistic fine-tuning, in which the same representation encodes one individual's genotype and methylation. A fine-tuned model can then make person-specific predictions from a single assay. Under this novel fine-tuning framework, we show that ModBERT effectively utilizes methylation information to classify peaks from functional genomic assays, including histone mark (n=11 different marks) and transcription factor binding (n=69 TFs) ChIP-seq data, outperforming ab initio trained models and ModBERT pretrained on sequences without methylation. In silico methylation perturbations yield TF sensitivities that correlate with independent methylation-aware motif models. Using an evaluation design that separates generalization to new loci from generalization to new individuals, ModBERT predicts chromatin accessibility at held-out loci in held-out individuals (AUROC 0.88). Its predicted variant effects agree with likely causal caQTLs (Spearman correlation = 0.52) but not with variants associated only through linkage, a traditionally challenging task. Overall, ModBERT establishes a framework for personal-genome language modeling, in which a model reads each individual's genetic and epigenetic sequence rather than a shared reference. This enables in silico dissection of variant and methylation effects on gene regulation and principled prioritization of candidates for experimental validation as population-scale long-read cohorts (e.g., 1KGP and Human Pangenome Reference Consortium) grow.

datasets_used: ChIP-seq transcription factor binding peaks (n=69 TFs)
llm.novelty_zh: 将个体基因型与CpG甲基化以概率化五字母（A/C/G/T/M）表示引入DNA语言模型，并提出概率微调以实现个人基因组级别的预测。
llm.summary_zh: ModBERT 是一个 DNA 语言模型，用五字母概率基因组表示同时编码群体等位基因频率和 CpG 甲基化水平，并基于 1000 Genomes 长读长数据进行软目标掩码语言模型预训练。该模型通过概率微调为单个个体的基因型和甲基化做个性化预测，在组蛋白标记与转录因子 ChIP-seq 峰分类、染色质可及性及 caQTL 效应预测上报告了结果。它属于基因组调控序列建模，与虚拟细胞主题只有间接关联。

title: Know Thy Neighbour: Benchmarking Protein Language Model Embedding-Based Annotation Reveals Anisotropy Substantially Impacts Retrieval
abstract: Functional annotation using protein language models (`pLMs') usually proceeds by transferring the function of a query's nearest neighbour in a reference database. A major drawback is that embedding-based annotation transfer has no null model, i.e. no accepted way to set a cosine-similarity threshold to control false positives. This contrasts with traditional bioinformatics methods, including sequence- and structure-based alignment tools, which rank hits with E-values derived from explicit null models. Here, we benchmark final-layer, mean-pooled embeddings from twelve models against MMseqs2 and Foldseek for remote-homology retrieval on curated datasets based on Swiss-Prot and SCOPe, fixing per-model thresholds at a 1% false-positive rate and probing the score with a ladder of synthetic decoys. On Swiss-Prot, pLMs without retrieval training recover at most 15% of remote homologs at this operating point, against 85% for MMseqs2, and for the ESM-2 and ESM-C families shuffled decoys have higher cosine similarities to their nearest database hits than real remote homologs do. These two pLM families exhibit extreme anisotropy, using fewer than 15 effective dimensions out of 640-2560, and low effective dimensionality is strongly associated with poor performance across models. Applying ZCA whitening, fit on the reference database, to the embeddings sharply raises threshold-free Top-1 superfamily retrieval, e.g. for ESM-2 650M from 59% to 88% on SCOPe, and generally improves remote homology sensitivity at a fixed false-positive rate. As correcting embedding anisotropy requires only the reference database and is compute cheap, it should be considered and tested for any pLM embedding-based annotation task.

llm.novelty_zh: 首次系统揭示蛋白语言模型（pLM）嵌入的各向异性（有效维度极低）是基于嵌入的功能注释检索失败的主因，并证明仅用参考库拟合的ZCA白化即可显著提升检索性能，同时在固定假阳性率下与MMseqs2和Foldseek进行对比。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作在 Swiss-Prot 和 SCOPe 构建的远源同源检索数据集上，以1%假阳性率为阈值，对十二种 pLM 的最终层均值池化嵌入与 MMseqs2、Foldseek 进行基准比较，并用合成诱饵序列检验相似度分数。结果显示 ESM-2 和 ESM-C 系列存在极端各向异性（有效维度不足15），低有效维度与检索性能差密切相关；对嵌入施加基于参考库的 ZCA 白化可大幅提升 Top-1 超家族检索（如 ESM-2 650M 在 SCOPe 上由59%升至88%）。该工作属于蛋白功能注释方法学，与虚拟细胞主题仅间接相关。

title: ProtCOVER: Family-Aware Conformal Prediction for Variant Effect Predictors on Unseen Protein Families
abstract: Protein language models and related variant effect predictors (VEPs) increasingly classify missense variants in proteins evolutionarily distant from those used for calibration. Split conformal prediction over variants is valid for its own target, a random variant dominated by well-studied families, but deployment needs coverage for a variant of a new family. On ProteinGym clinical substitutions with five zero-shot predictors, Mondrian conformal comes within 0.005 of that target for four predictors, yet family-weighted pathogenic coverage is only 0.823-0.873 at a 0.90 target for all five, without any shift. We present ProtCOVER, a conformal procedure that treats homology families, rather than individual variants, as the exchangeable unit. ProtCOVER (i) calibrates at the family level over label-free homology clusters, giving marginal coverage for a new family under family exchangeability; (ii) adapts to descriptor shift by calibrating conditionally on an estimated density ratio of label-free descriptors (sequence similarity, alignment depth and embedding distance; a variant reweights by the ratio instead), with finite-sample family-weighted coverage, valid as computed, whenever the true ratio is a nonnegative affine function of the estimate; and (iii) can abstain at low effective calibration support, which proved no better than random abstention. Under a shift of its descriptors, ProtCOVER's mean worse-class shortfall below the target is 0.000, against 0.010 for group-weighted and 0.029 for hierarchical conformal prediction, with larger sets (about equal at matched coverage); on orphan families and held-out embedding regions it matches group weighting (0.002 against 0.003). In evaluations following pre-registered protocols, every shift-aware method met the target on new ClinVar variants of benchmark proteins, which ESM-1b separated better; on 12,225 proteins outside the benchmark, every method fell short for pathogenic variants with either of two predictors, ProtCOVER and a variant conditioned on the descriptors the least, within the 0.01 margin of group weighting.

llm.novelty_zh: 将共形预测的可交换单位从单个变异提升为同源家族，并用基于描述符密度比的加权来应对分布偏移，以保证对新蛋白家族中致病变异的覆盖率。
llm.summary_zh: 该文针对蛋白语言模型等变异效应预测器（VEP）在进化上遥远的新蛋白家族上覆盖率不足的问题，提出 ProtCOVER：以同源家族而非单个变异作为共形预测的可交换单位，并基于标签无关描述符的密度比进行条件校准。在 ProteinGym 临床替换数据上，作者报告其在描述符偏移下的最差类别覆盖缺口更小，并在预注册协议的外部评测中检验了方法表现。该工作与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型关系较弱，主要属于蛋白变异预测的不确定性校准方法学。

title: Spatial causal discovery reveals novel mechanisms of cellular senescence in human liver
abstract: The complex network of mechanisms that surround cellular senescence, such as its precise causes and effects, are not entirely understood at present. Senescence occurs when a cell permanently ceases dividing, halts apoptosis, stops performing its normal functions, and begins secreting chemicals that can induce other cells in its environment to also become senescent. Senescent cells are present in both healthy and unhealthy tissue, but their abundance is positively correlated with disease and age. A better understanding of senescence could lead to healthier aging, improved recovery from chemotherapy, or increased lifespan. This study used novel machine learning algorithms - with guaranteed properties of correctness under broad assumptions - to investigate senescence in human liver tissue by analyzing Visium spatial transcriptomics data. This produced data-driven models of the causes and effects of senescence, both locally and from nearby tissue. This report includes an assessment of whether the data meet key requirements for causal analysis, the transcripts identified by causal analyses as causes and effects of senescence marker genes, and pathway analyses of those gene sets.

datasets_used: Visium spatial transcriptomics human liver data
llm.novelty_zh: 将具有正确性保证的因果发现算法应用于 Visium 空间转录组数据，以推断人肝脏中衰老标记基因的局部及邻近组织因果来源与效应。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究使用具有理论保证的因果发现算法分析人肝脏 Visium 空间转录组数据，构建衰老的局部及邻域因果模型，并检验数据是否满足因果分析的关键前提。研究还识别了与衰老标记基因有因果关联的转录本，并对这些基因集进行通路分析。该工作主要聚焦衰老机制的因果推断，与虚拟细胞的扰动建模只有间接关联。

title: Spectrast: a multiscale spatial statistics toolkit for single-cell spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves gene expression in physical space, but the spatial statistics typically used to quantify spatial organization scale poorly to imaging-based datasets with hundreds-of-thousands of cells and thousands of genes. We recast the standard spatial-autocorrelation statistics as convolutions on a rasterized representation of the gene expression matrix and evaluate them with the fast Fourier transform. Measuring spatial statistics across multiple length scales becomes tractable for every gene using this approach, which extends naturally to differential reorganization testing between two tissue conditions.

llm.novelty_zh: 将经典空间自相关统计量重写为基因表达矩阵栅格化后的卷积，并用快速傅里叶变换（FFT）计算，使多尺度空间统计可扩展到大规模成像型空间转录组数据，并支持两种组织条件间的差异空间重组检验。

title: Learning gene co-regulation across cells with Multicellular Transformer
abstract: Understanding how genes coordinate across cells is central to explaining tissue function and disease, yet most existing models still take a single cell as input and therefore emphasize cell-intrinsic regulation. We present the Multicellular Transformer (MCT), a foundation model built around a different assumption: cells function together within tissues, so the appropriate unit of input is not one cell in isolation but a set of cells from the same sample. By jointly modeling multiple cells, MCT learns context-aware gene embeddings that capture gene-gene interactions across the tissue environment. Trained on a large set of tissue samples (>4200) across more than 30 tissue types, MCT recovers ligand-receptor interactions, infers cross-cell signaling programs, and reveals spatial co-localization patterns directly from scRNA-seq data. Its contextual embeddings identify disease-specific rewiring of gene neighborhoods in systemic lupus erythematosus and COVID-19 and predict population-level perturbation effects in cancer without additional training. By linking gene-level regulation to tissue-scale organization, MCT provides a scalable framework for modeling multicellular biology and enables in silico discovery of therapeutic targets and tissue-specific dependencies.

llm.novelty_zh: 将基础模型的输入单位从单细胞扩展为同一样本内的一组细胞，从而学习反映组织环境的上下文感知基因嵌入，并支持无需额外训练的群体层面扰动预测。
llm.summary_zh: Multicellular Transformer (MCT) 以同一样本中的一组细胞作为输入进行联合建模，在 4200 余个跨 30 多种组织的样本上预训练，学习上下文相关的基因嵌入。摘要称其能够直接从 scRNA-seq 中恢复配体-受体相互作用、跨细胞信号程序和空间共定位模式，并在系统性红斑狼疮和 COVID-19 中揭示疾病相关的基因邻域重连。该模型还可在无额外训练的情况下预测癌症中的群体层面扰动效应。

title: GatorAnchor: Cross-Modal Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Reliable Cell Neighborhoods in Single-Cell Multi-Omics
abstract: Cross-modal uncertainty challenges single-cell multi-omics integration because molecular modalities differ in sparsity, technical noise, and context-dependent biological informativeness, producing discordant cell-cell relationships. Treating conflicting evidence as equally reliable can propagate uncertain relationships and obscure biologically meaningful cellular heterogeneity. GatorAnchor is a cross-modal uncertainty-aware framework that learns modality-specific probabilistic representations, quantifies disagreement across modalities and neighborhood evidence sources, and refines cell-cell relationships according to their reliability. Across ten paired transcriptome-protein and transcriptome-chromatin datasets, GatorAnchor achieves the highest mean performance across four evaluation metrics among nine representative integration methods, demonstrating improved resolution of cellular heterogeneity. Candidate relations with greater composite unreliability show lower consistency with reference cell-type structure, whereas filtering highly unreliable relations increases same-type edge purity across all datasets. Modality conflict is associated with transcript-protein measurement discordance, while transcriptome-chromatin analyses reveal lineage-dependent contributions of molecular and decoder-derived evidence. A three-modality transcriptome-chromatin-protein analysis characterizes cluster of differentiation 4 (CD4)-related communities with distinct molecular profiles and consistent within-donor contrasts across 12 donors. Under incomplete and mosaic measurements, GatorAnchor preserves informative cell-population structure, while cross-modal correspondence increasingly depends on paired-cell anchors. These findings support uncertainty-aware neighborhood refinement for reliable and interpretable characterization of cellular heterogeneity.

title: Decompose and Recompose: Reference-Centered Multimodal Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Enzyme Turnover Prediction
abstract: Predicting enzyme turnover numbers ($k_{\mathrm{cat}}$) from protein sequences and reaction chemistry supports virtual screening, which requires distinguishing activity differences between enzyme--reaction pairs. Recent interaction models face two representation challenges. First, they merge reactants and products before enzyme interaction, leaving separate enzyme responses implicit despite the two sides' distinct roles in recognition, transformation, and release. Second, cross-attention readouts mix reaction-dependent changes with an enzyme-specific residue background, which can obscure activity-relevant differences across samples. To address these challenges, we introduce EnzRef, a lightweight framework for multimodal adaptation of frozen protein language models. EnzRef decomposes reaction chemistry into reactant and product conditions, models their interactions with the enzyme separately, and recomposes the resulting responses for activity prediction. During these interactions, Reference-Centered Cross-Attention expresses each response as a deviation from the enzyme's own residue background to expose chemically conditioned differences for activity discrimination. With 1.72M trainable parameters, EnzRef achieves state-of-the-art source prediction on CatPred-DB and zero-shot transfer to TurNuP-DB. Across ten independent runs, EnzRef achieves 19.8\% higher mean $R^2$ than the strongest baseline MCKcat in zero-shot transfer to unseen enzymes. It also predicts activity differences more accurately between pairs sharing an enzyme or a reaction.
affiliations: Faculty of Applied Sciences, Macao Polytechnic University, Macao SAR, China

title: Transferring CRISPRi knockdown responses to new cell lines requires screening part of each line
abstract: Perturb-seq screens measure knockdown responses in one cell line at a time. Models that transfer responses to new lines rarely beat simple averages, and standard metrics often ignore noise. It is unclear how much of a response is shared and what a new line must contribute. We studied CRISPR interference Perturb-seq of essential genes in four human cell lines, using noise ceilings and calibrated metrics. We also introduce CASTER, a set-based model that adapts the transferred mean to the target line. After noise correction, responses correlated at a median of 0.52, highest between the TP53 wild-type lines. With 30% of a line screened, a linear model and CASTER scored 0.84 and 0.80 versus 0.44 for the transferred mean (1 equals a technical duplicate). CASTER led only at 2.5% screened (0.62 versus 0.47) and fell below the transferred mean without a screen. Response size tracked general essentiality more than line-specific dependency.

title: SpaceMACE: Spatially-Aware Tumour Cell Annotation for Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract: Accurate discrimination between tumour and non-tumour cells is essential for interpreting spatial transcriptomics data and identifying spatially resolved therapeutic targets. Existing tumour-cell annotation approaches were primarily developed for single-cell RNA sequencing and do not explicitly incorporate the spatial organization of cells. Here, we introduce SpaceMACE, an extension of the MACE tumour-cell annotation framework for sequencing-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. SpaceMACE first combines reference-based cell-type classification with copy-number-variation-based tumour classification. The resulting consensus annotations are subsequently refined using spatial proximity and gene-expression similarity. We evaluated SpaceMACE across multiple spatial transcriptomics platforms, including Stereo-seq, Visium HD, CosMx and Xenium, and across colorectal, hepatocellular and ovarian cancer datasets. SpaceMACE retained the high precision of the original MACE framework while improving the spatial coherence of tumour-cell annotations. Together, these results demonstrate that SpaceMACE provides a scalable and platform-independent framework for tumour-cell annotation in spatial transcriptomics and supports the spatial investigation of tumour-specific molecular targets.

title: Pluripotent and differentiated cells display distinct genomic and nuclear landscapes of genome folding variability
abstract: Chromosome folding varies between cells. It is not known whether cell types differ in the extent of folding variability, whether distinct chromosomal regions in the same cell type display different levels of variability, and how folding variability relates to sub-nuclear location and gene expression. We combined two single-cell Hi-C approaches with 3D genome modeling of pseudo-single cells (IGM), DNA FISH, chromosome painting, and single-cell RNA-seq across a five-stage differentiation trajectory from human embryonic stem cells to hepatocyte-like cells. In all cell types folding variability correlates with compartment status, is highest towards the nuclear interior, decreases as a function of radial position in the nucleus, and is the lowest at the periphery. Loci associated with nuclear landmarks such as speckles, and especially the nuclear periphery display more consistent subnuclear positioning in all cell stages. Moreover, pluripotent and differentiated cells display different overall levels of chromosome folding variability: in H1 pluripotent cells the entire genome displays higher folding and positional variability. In contrast, in differentiated cells folding variability is generally lower along the genome and the number of loci that become consistently positioned at the nuclear periphery increases sharply. The two distinct patterns of folding variability were correlated with cell-to-cell gene expression variation: In pluripotent cells gene expression variation is large, pervasive and seen throughout the genome and the nucleus. In differentiated cells cell-to-cell variation in gene expression is much lower and restricted mostly to genes located near the center of the nucleus, consistent with the restricted pattern of chromosome folding variation. These findings reveal two distinct genomic states: pluripotent cells maintain a variably folded, spatially permissive genome and transcriptional plasticity, whereas differentiated cells mature into a spatially deterministic, more consistently folded organization that correlates with more restricted transcriptional programs.
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School

title: A spatial correlation function approach reveals zonation loss in liver disease
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures the expression of hundreds to thousands of genes in each cell together with the cell's position in the tissue. Here we use spatial correlation functions, which describe how the correlation of gene expression between cells decays with distance, to quantify how the spatial organization of gene expression changes in disease. From the correlation function of each gene, or of each pair of genes, we extract two numbers: a susceptibility, which measures how strongly gene expression is correlated between nearby cells, and a correlation length, the distance over which this correlation extends. Both are in physical units and can be compared directly between samples and conditions. We apply the approach to healthy and fibrotic mouse liver using newly generated data, and to healthy and fibrotic human liver using published data. Correlations between gene pairs identify genes of the same hepatocyte zone, and assign a zone to 1,266 genes that are not known zonation markers. The two fibrotic conditions differ: CCl4 injection in mice produces a moderate reorganization in which some genes lose spatial correlation and others gain it, while in human fibrosis almost every measured gene loses it. Changes in spatial correlation are only weakly related to changes in expression level. For instance Cyp2c29 and Pon1 partially lose their spatial correlation in treated mice, although their average expression does not consistently fall. Spatial correlation functions therefore detect changes in tissue organization that measurements of expression level alone miss.

title: Cell-state conditioning predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects
abstract: Background: Second-generation sequence models can be conditioned on a cell state supplied as a single-cell snapshot rather than selected from a fixed catalogue, but whether that conditioning carries an experimentally applied perturbation has not been tested. Results: We conditioned such a model on interferon-{beta}-stimulated and unstimulated monocytes from a published experiment, using cells disjoint from those providing the measurement, and asked whether the predicted expression response tracks the measured one and whether the same conditioning identifies expression QTL specific to the stimulated state. Predicted and measured responses agree at Spearman {rho} = 0.616 across 119 genes (95% CI 0.486 to 0.716), and at 0.607 after all 119 target genes are deleted from the conditioning input; across fifteen conditions the model's response scales with how much each condition's biology genuinely overlaps the target response (slope 0.73, Pearson 0.92), and a near-neighbour monocyte subset receives 0.295 against a measured overlap of 0.336. For stimulation-specific genetic effects we find no reliable evidence: the pre-specified primary arm moves from p = 0.0019 to 0.443 once both conditions must carry a measurable predicted effect, and the separation localises to the resting-condition baseline. Neither model generation's catalogue contains a perturbed sample, 0 of 4,430 tracks and 0 of 2,799 conditions, although both carry activation-state labels, so the gap is experimental perturbation rather than cell state. Two incidental findings apply beyond this model: credible-set membership mislabels over half of putatively condition-specific loci, and gating a ratio statistic on its larger term manufactures signal. Conclusions: Conditioning therefore conveys the state but not the mechanism: transfer between states is supported at the level of expression and unsupported at the level of variant effect, and an evaluation that separates the two is needed before either is claimed.
affiliations: Department and Institute of Urology, Hubei Provincial Clinical Research Center for Minimally Invasive Treatment of Urology, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical Coll

title: S-PLM-TM enables fast and accurate sequence-based search for remote homologs
abstract: Protein structures and functions can remain conserved after extensive sequence divergence, but detecting these distant relationships across large databases remains challenging. Here we present S-PLM-TM, a sequence-only remote homology search tool based on a structure-aware protein language model. Cross-modal flow matching and contrastive learning incorporate structural information into sequence representations. A lightweight calibration head enables structural-similarity search with the frozen encoder, while a residue-level alignment head generates structural alignments directly from sequence. S-PLM-TM outperforms the tested sequence-based methods in remote homology detection, rivals structure-based methods in structural classification and retrieves the most functionally consistent neighbors. It also retrieves distantly related enzymes with shared catalytic functions at a level comparable to the best-performing structure-based methods. In large-scale database search, S-PLM-TM achieves the highest average precision among both sequence-based and alignment-free methods, with speed approaching the fastest sequence-alignment tools. Together, these results establish S-PLM-TM as a practical tool that combines sensitive and biologically informative remote homology search with the speed required for database-scale retrieval.

title: An interpretable framework for decoding transcriptomic foundation models
abstract: Background: What transcriptomic foundation models encode, and how well they describe cells and tissue on targeted spatial panels, is under-explored. It is unclear whether a concept-labeled sparse autoencoder (SAE) feature represents its concept or only the genes it detects. Results: Here, we propose interpreTFM, which decomposes frozen transcriptomic foundation model activations with SAEs. We applied it to a CosMx lung-cancer section, four further CosMx donors, and a Xenium renal-cell-carcinoma section. On held-out tokens of known genes, sparse features marked 262--593 concepts per analysis layer, and SAEs of re-initialized scGPT and Geneformer did as well. On held-out genes, concept F1 was 0.01--0.12 for every representation and lowest for sparse features. A linear probe of hidden states predicted the concepts of unseen genes, but only in trained models. Per cell, sparse features reached 66--98\% of single-gene population specificity (57--110\% in the donors). In the analyzed CosMx section, sparse-feature niches matched author cell types at ARI 0.34--0.42, while expression-only niches reached 0.30; in the donors, their defining concepts recurred but their composition did not. In Xenium, the niches shared by all models were recovered from expression alone. Calibrated model interface calls were at chance in CosMx and tracked transcript spillover in Xenium. Conclusions: On these panels, SAE features act as concept-labeled gene detectors, while learned concept information is distributed across hidden dimensions. Concept labels should be checked against held-out genes and re-initialized models. For cells and niches, the features give named descriptions, comparable across models and patients and bounded by the measured panel.
affiliations: Department of Computer Science, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA; Department of Biomedical Engineering, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, USA

title: Persistent DNA damage reprograms the cutaneous microenvironment into a stress-responsive immunometabolic pro-pigmentary niche
abstract: Chronic ultraviolet (UV) exposure induces progressive pigmentary remodeling of the skin, yet how persistent DNA damage influences tissue-level responses remains poorly understood. Xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group C (XP-C), characterized by defective global genome nucleotide excision repair, provides a model to investigate these processes. Here, integrating chronic UVB irradiation of Xpc-deficient mice with spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics profiling, and functional analyses, we identify a coordinated multicellular response associated with persistent hyperpigmentation. UVB-exposed Xpc-deficient skin exhibited increased eumelanin accumulation, altered melanosome organization, enhanced melanosome transfer to keratinocytes, and regional melanocyte expansion. Proteomic, metabolomic, and kinomic analyses revealed coordinated alterations in inflammatory, cytoskeletal, redox, metabolic, and pigmentation-associated programs. Spatial transcriptomics further identified distinct keratinocyte states and inflammatory immune niches enriched in hyperpigmented regions, coinciding with increased melanocyte abundance and DNA damage. These findings suggest that pigmentary remodeling occurs within a spatially organized, stress-responsive immunometabolic tissue environment rather than reflecting melanocyte-intrinsic alterations alone. Analyses of human XP-C skin and XPC-deficient primary human melanocytes revealed overlapping pigmentation-associated, inflammatory, and cytoskeletal alterations, supporting the relevance of these observations to human disease. Together, our findings reveal a previously underappreciated relationship between persistent DNA damage and spatially coordinated multicellular remodeling, providing a framework for understanding how defective genome maintenance is associated with chronic pigmentary changes and altered tissue homeostasis. These findings may also offer insights into the mechanisms underlying common acquired hyperpigmentary disorders.

title: Pharmacological and genetic access to astrocytic cholesterol programs in human neural cells
abstract: Astrocyte-neuron interactions coordinate cholesterol metabolism, cell adhesion, and synaptic gene expression, and related gene expression programs decline together in schizophrenia. Whether pharmacological or genetic perturbations can selectively engage components of this coordinated biology was unknown. Here we combine genetically diverse cultures of human stem-cell-derived neurons and astrocytes, pharmacological profiling, genetic association mapping and CRISPR interference to examine these biological programs. In stem-cell-derived astrocyte mono-cultures, the antipsychotic clozapine induced a focused transcriptional response involving cholesterol biosynthesis and export, and drove an increase in intracellular and secreted cholesterol. This response overlapped with the cholesterol-related component of the astrocytic response to neuronal contact seen in neuron-astrocyte co-cultures, but did not extend to synaptic cell-adhesion genes. In neuron-astrocyte co-cultures, clozapine also increased neuronal firing. Across individual cell donors, cholesterol-pathway induction by clozapine was broadly shared but varied in magnitude. Gene-expression patterns in untreated donors were associated with differential responses to clozapine and the liver X receptor agonist GW3965. Common genetic variation influenced expression of several cholesterol-related genes, including a clozapine-dependent association of HSD17B7 expression with nearby genetic variants. Independently, repression of LDLR induced coordinated expression of cholesterol-biosynthesis genes in astrocytes that overlapped with astrocyte responses to clozapine and neuronal contact. These findings identify shared cholesterol-related transcriptional responses to pharmacological and genetic perturbations and link common genetic variation to distinct features of cholesterol-pathway responses.

title: DRAFT: graph-recurrent learning of dynamic gene regulatory networks along single-cell multi-omics trajectories
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness. In mouse cellular reprogramming and Drosophila adult spermatogenesis, it recovers interactions supported by independent ChIP-seq, perturbation and Hi-C data, together with known stage-specific regulators. By inferring regulatory activity from dynamic network structure rather than expression alone, DRAFT identifies regulators whose activity precedes their transcriptional peak, including the candidate early germline regulator Mondo. Germline-specific Mondo knockdown alters germline stem cell number and expression of the predicted targets kuz and mamo. DRAFT also enables nonlinear alignment of co-developing lineages and reveals stage-specific cell-cell communication.
affiliations: Centre for organismal Studies (COS), Heidelberg University

title: Model evaluation metrics of Virtual Cell Challenge 2026
abstract: Virtual cell models aim to predict the effects of genetic, environmental, chemical and other perturbations in silico, reducing the dependency on complex and costly experiments. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 motivates the field toward this goal, tasking models with zero-shot prediction of the transcriptional responses to CRISPRi knockdowns in six human cell lines. The faithfulness of a model to the experiment is assessed by metrics that compare its predictions with the real data, and designing such metrics is not trivial. We developed the metrics of the 2026 Challenge around three principles: a metric should (i) reflect the biological information extracted from experiments, (ii) be calibrated on a repeat of the experiment, and (iii) resist shortcut solutions that raise the score without predicting the response. Here we present the six resulting metrics, the reasoning behind each of them, and their evaluations on the Challenge data. Two of the metrics compare the pseudobulk expression profiles of predicted and measured cells, while four assess the genes that respond to each perturbation, the central readout of a Perturb-seq experiment. The metrics are implemented in cell-eval2, an open-source Python package. On the Challenge data, all six metrics score a repeat of the experiment above the mean baseline, and the shortcut solutions that the metrics of the 2025 Challenge left open can no longer raise the score. The new metrics are therefore more robust than the previous ones.
affiliations: Arc Institute, Palo Alto, CA, USA

title: Sc-HistoMorphomics: A General Framework for High-throughput, Multimodal Profiling of Nuclear Morphology in Tissues.
abstract: Quantitative cellular morphology provides a rich but underutilized window into cell identity and state. We introduce sc-HistoMorphomics, a scalable framework for profiling nuclear morphology in whole-slide H&E images and correlating these measurements with spatial transcriptomics data. Our pipeline combines deep-learning based segmentation with 194 interpretable morphometric features capturing nuclear shape, eosin and hematoxylin texture, and neighbourhood architecture, enabling high-throughput, multimodal characterization of tissue organization. Applied to endometrium, breast cancer tissue, and pancreas, sc-HistoMorphomics revealed conserved high-dimensional feature structure across tissues and reproducible association between morphology and gene expression. Eosin-based texture features were associated with senescence signatures in endometrium, and morphology-based clustering recapitulated broad stromal, lymphocyte, and epithelial tumor cell classes in breast cancer. In pancreas, negative correlations between CDKN1A and multiple morphological features were consistent across cell types and donors. Together, these results establish sc-HistoMorphomics as a generalizable and interpretable tool for linking morphology with spatially resolved molecular state across diverse tissues.

title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
abstract: Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability. Results: We present ARC-Impute, which regularises cell-to-spot mapping through anchor-residual optimisation, target-guided reference curation and routing, and twin-panel consistency. Across 17 human and mouse datasets spanning spot-based and single-cell technologies, ARC-Impute ranked first for held-out Pearson correlation throughout and exceeded the dataset-specific baseline mean by 47.3% on average. It also achieved the strongest spot-level cell-type composition recovery across three pseudospot benchmarks and retained leading accuracy and consistency under reference and training-gene perturbations. Cross-validated predictions revealed systematic differences in gene imputability. Availability and implementation: Code and workflows at https://github.com/ethanhaan/arc-impute.
affiliations: School of Mathematics and Statistics, The University of Sydney, Australia

title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A, respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.
affiliations: Center for Genomics of Neurodegenerative Disease, New York Genome Center, 101 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10013; Department of Neurology, Columbia Univ

title: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable. Here we present CIRCA (Causal Interaction Representation for Cellular Architectures), a self-supervised causal representation learning framework that jointly learns identifiable cell- and neighborhood-level transcriptional programs and the directed interactions among them under explicit assumptions. It can also be extended to incorporate additional modalities such as pathology. Benchmarked against five existing methods across seven cell-resolution datasets, CIRCA achieved the highest biological accuracy in six and the highest overall score in all five multi-section datasets, while recovering higher-order anatomical organization. In an AD mouse model, incorporating amyloid-{beta} pathology revealed four region-specific plaque niches enriched for microglia. Plaque-associated microglia shared a core disease-associated response whose strength varied by region, and AD genetic risk was preferentially enriched in hippocampal and cortical plaque-associated microglia. Reproducible latent factors linked to cell-level amyloid burden separated phagocytic from inflammatory microglial programs. Applied to a human colorectal cancer dataset, CIRCA resolved patient-specific tumor niches, conserved stromal remodeling niches, and distinct macrophage states, highlighting its versatility. Together, these results establish CIRCA as a methodological advance over existing approaches, enabling deeper insights into tissue organization and the molecular dependencies linking cells to their local environments.
affiliations: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
abstract: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq. Building on this resource, we develop GenVinci, a multimodal tissue foundation model that reconstructs 3D tissue scenes from routine 2D histology. GenVinci predicts spatial gene expression from H&E with zero-shot generalization and maps senescence-associated states across 85.8 million cells, revealing cell-type-specific patterns and disease-associated remodeling. Integration with human genetics implicates suprabasal keratinocytes in atopic dermatitis and keratinocyte carcinomas, linked to higher and lower p16 and p21 expression, respectively. These findings establish GenVinci as a framework mapping senescence in 3D across scales.
affiliations: Cutaneous Biology Research Center, Massachusetts General Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA, U

title: spicyR enables robust, well-powered co-localisation tests in large spatial omics cohorts
abstract: Spatial omics technologies can now profile finely resolved cell populations in patient tissue at scale, offering a way to link their arrangement to outcomes. Yet images often differ in size, shape and cell content, and existing tests between patient groups mistake these differences for co-localisation or weight every image equally. We present spicyR v2, which avoids both problems with a fast, permutation-free test that accounts for these differences and weights each image by how precisely it measures co-localisation. In simulations and 74 analyses of 42 public datasets, it controlled false discoveries, had more power than spicyR v1 and was robust to tears, holes and differences in cell number that misled other methods. These analyses also revealed that many studies relating co-localisation to clinical outcomes are underpowered, and spicyR v2 can estimate the number of patients a new study needs. spicyR v2 analyses 100 million cells in minutes, making robust, well-powered tests of co-localisation practical for large spatial omics cohorts.

title: MARRI: Mechanism-Aware Learning of RNA-RNA Interactions with Foundation Models
abstract: RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) are central to post-transcriptional regulation, yet their prediction requires accounting for structural accessibility and intermolecular base pairing beyond sequence complementarity. Pretrained RNA foundation models provide representations of individual RNAs, but translating these representations into interaction predictions requires mechanistic knowledge of interaction recognition. Here, we introduce MARRI, a mechanism-aware multimodal framework that couples pretrained representations with domain knowledge by embedding learned opening penalties and hybridization gains into bidirectional cross-RNA attention. MARRI improves ROC--AUC and PR--AUC over the strongest baseline by 12.20\% and 10.25\%, respectively, and maintains strong discrimination for unseen RNA partnerships and interaction regions. Perturbation and repeat-context analyses identify prediction-relevant sequence regions. Integrating MARRI-derived interaction propensities with disease-associated expression profiles links molecular prediction to systems-level models of disease progression and network remodeling. MARRI thus illustrates a knowledge-guided strategy for coupling molecular foundation models with domain knowledge to support grounded prediction, interpretation and systems-level hypothesis generation.

title: CellVADIS: Inferring cross-tissue immune cell trafficking dynamics from single-cell snapshots
abstract: The ability of immune cells to traffic between and enter different tissues is an important hallmark for effective immune responses. However, despite advances in high-throughput single-cell profiling, identifying circulating cell populations that drive tissue-specific immunity remains elusive. Here we present CellVADIS, an optimal transport based computational framework to infer cross-tissue immune cell dynamics. By connecting single-cell measurements across tissue sites, CellVADIS enables the prediction of cell migration fates, characterization of tissue-specific trafficking signatures on circulating cells, as well as identification of tissue entry points. We benchmarked our method against synthetic data and applied CellVADIS to two cross-tissue single-cell datasets which revealed characteristic marker expression patterns that define tissue-specific trafficking signatures and homing niches of tissue-entering CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. CellVADIS provides a flexible, open-source tool for identifying cross-tissue single-cell dynamics from various high-throughput single-cell measurements, which would support the design of vaccination and immunotherapeutic regimens to generate tissue-specific immunity.

title: Prediction and Dissection of Nitrogenase Activity Based on Protein Sequences using Dual Descriptor
abstract: Nitrogenase reduces N2 to ammonia at ambient temperature and pressure, but its activity differs markedly among natural sequences, and conventional wet-laboratory screening suffers from low throughput and long turnaround times. Existing computational methods have partially alleviated this bottleneck, yet most of them rely on protein embeddings obtained from protein language models together with features such as gene expression, and their interpretability analyses mostly stop at the level of feature contribution. Here we present CarmnaDD, a purely sequence-driven framework built on the dual descriptor (DD): two learnable components, the composition weight map (CWM) and the position weight function (PWF), jointly generate a position-resolved description N(k), so that activity can be predicted without any prior knowledge beyond the sequence. On the same dataset used by Carmna, CarmnaDD attains R2 = 0.60 for regression and AUC = 0.94 and F1 = 0.86 for classification, better than our previous Carmna, which integrates multiple features. Interpretability analysis shows that the amplitude of the periodic terms of the PWF decreases as the rank increases, indicating that the positional encoding strategy adapts to the rank; the high-weight 3-mer fragments in the CWM are significantly enriched in polar uncharged residues, which corroborates the SHAP-based conclusion of Carmna; sliding-window scanning identifies fragments significantly associated with activity (FDR < 0.05), and the strongest window displays a D-X-E pattern with conserved flanks and a polymorphic center, sequences carrying R at the central position showing the highest activity; conservation is significantly negatively correlated ({rho} = -0.30) with description intensity. Mapping the key windows onto the protein structure shows that four highly correlated windows converge on the nucleotide-binding interface and the conformational-transmission/protein-docking interface of NifH. These results provide a purely sequence-based framework for nitrogenase activity prediction that balances performance and interpretability.

title: Gene regulatory networks and the organization of cell differentiation in multicellular organisms
abstract: Across their development, clonal multicellular organisms generate new cell types from less differentiated cell types. Differentiation pathways arrange into a hierarchical, tree-like organization: regressions from specialized to undifferentiated cell types rarely occur and undifferentiated cell types often have the potential to produce, when subject to distinct stimuli, two or more differently specialized cell types. How cell type transitions acquire such a peculiar disposition requires an explanation that must reside in the properties of gene regulatory networks (GRNs); after all, GRNs orchestrate the changes in gene activity that define cell types. We studied vast numbers of small dynamic model networks to search for elementary GRNs that could yield the simplest hierarchical, developmental-like, differentiation patterns. We found that only a small minority of GRNs are compatible with hierarchical cell type transitions. Importantly, GRNs that yielded developmental-like differentiation patterns shared common traits: One is the presence of tangles of cycles of positive interactions. Genes in such a tangle produce an all-or-none one-way response to a signal. Another such trait is mutual inhibition between genes associated to different specialized cell types, enforcing their mutually exclusive activation. Moreover, these regulatory patterns are more abundant in published experimentally sustained developmental GRNs than as expected by chance. In addition, we show that it is easy to maintain hierarchical cellular differentiation throughout evolution, even when undergoing changes in gene regulatory interactions and developmental mechanisms. Our work supports the prevalence of design principles that organize hierarchically differentiation pathways in clonal multicellular organisms.
affiliations: Universidad Autonoma de San Luis Potosi

title: Causal regulators of human T-cell and macrophage activation from perturbation screens, and a replicated coupling of T-cell exhaustion markers with macrophage M1 activation in patients under checkpoint blockade
abstract: Engineering anti-tumour immunity requires knowing which genes control T-cell and macrophage programs, and how the two compartments relate to each other in patients. We built ImmunoTwin, an analysis framework that addresses both questions with public data and with every test, baseline and criterion fixed before the result was computed. From a genome-scale CRISPR-interference Perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells (22 million cells, four donors) we derive a map of regulators of the cytotoxic effector program that is calibrated, reverses direction under CRISPR activation (rho = -0.53), and tracks interferon-gamma production among the hits of independent sorting-based screens (rho = 0.69). From a Perturb-seq in primary human macrophages we recover the TLR4-NF-kappaB pathway as regulator of the lipopolysaccharide response (pathway-level P = 0.0004) and find that transcriptional effects track TNF protein measured in independent donors (rho = 0.58). In both cell types, however, a generic measure of perturbation strength recovers the hits of functional screens better than the program-specific effect (area under the ROC curve 0.96 versus 0.73 in T cells; 0.87 versus 0.72 in macrophages). In 90 patients from seven cohorts with tumour sampled before and during checkpoint blockade, T-cell and macrophage programs shifted together, most strongly T-cell exhaustion markers and the macrophage M1 program (r = 0.43). Fixed as a hypothesis and tested once in 86 further patients from six cohorts, this association replicated (r = 0.51, permutation P = 0.0001) and was specific against expression-matched random gene sets (P = 0.004). The baseline state of one compartment did not improve the forecast of the other, so the criterion we had set for calling the framework a patient-level digital twin was not met. ImmunoTwin provides two validated perturbation maps, a replicated cross-compartment association in patients, and a caution on how such maps are benchmarked.

title: PDAC BioPortal: An Integrated Web Resource for Multi-Scale Analysis of Pancreatic Cancer Transcriptomics
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound cellular heterogeneity and treatment-associated remodeling, yet bulk, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomic datasets remain fragmented across separate portals. We developed PDAC BioPortal, an open-access, browser-based web resource integrating four complementary human PDAC cohorts: primary tumor versus normal pancreas (TCGA-PAAD and GTEx, n = 345), a neoadjuvant stereotactic body radiotherapy-containing bulk cohort (GSE225767, n = 55), a single-nucleus chemoradiotherapy atlas (GSE202051, 224,988 nuclei across 43 patients), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics (GSE274103, 23,436 spots across five tumors). The platform provides interactive differential expression, rank-based pathway enrichment, patient-level pseudobulk comparisons, survival exploration, and spatial visualization, alongside PDACopilot, a deterministic, evidence-grounded natural-language query interface. Across cohorts, neoadjuvant-treated bulk and single-nucleus pathway rankings showed significant concordance, while Kitagawa-Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition and compositional sensitivity testing separated epithelial debulking from cell-intrinsic signaling shifts. Interrogation of the NRF2-associated redox network illustrated how bulk changes diverge from cell-type-resolved and spatial patterns, while continuous Cox modeling linked higher NRF2-signature expression to shorter overall survival. PDAC BioPortal is freely available at https://limboper89.github.io/PAAD-SBRT-GEx-Dashboard/. Availability: https://limboper89.github.io/PAAD-SBRT-GEx-Dashboard/

title: Curated annotations locate biological concepts in protein language models from layers to neurons
abstract: Interpretability methods describe what a network has learned, yet their claims are rarely tested against model-independent ground truth. We argue that proteins are an ideal modality for interpretability since curators annotate functional sites residue by residue. Across three ESMC protein language models (300M-6B parameters), we show that conclusions depend on where models are read, how concepts are decoded, which units are examined, and how they are scored. Concepts become linearly readable along depth long before erasure impairs masked-token prediction, and 20-fold scaling shifts concept depth more than peak score. Most of a nonlinear probe's lead over a linear one reflects fitting and readout shape rather than nonlinear encoding. Over whole proteins, saturated metrics render feed-forward neurons indistinguishable from random rotations. At annotated residues, dual-signed neuron poles identify 2.5-5.4 times as many concepts as rotations without training, though sparse autoencoders identify more. Without held-out validation, however, shuffled annotations label nearly every latent, and causal reliance emerges in neuron groups rather than single poles. Reading selected intra-block states exposes binding and active sites that stream probes read poorly and lifts a simple probe 5% above the best published MCC on a leakage-controlled interaction benchmark. We recommend reading a model directly against annotation, scoring units where they fire with a measure that is not saturated, and training a dictionary only where it adds coverage.
affiliations: Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Delaware

title: Modelling Phenotypic Assay Noise for Multivariable Biomarker Discovery using Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Accurately predicting cancer drug response remains a major challenge in precision oncology. Although some therapies are guided by clinically-approved biomarkers, these markers often yield limited predictive value and are unavailable for many drugs. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning approaches trained on large-scale cancer cell line pharmacogenomic screens offer a promising route to more comprehensive response prediction, yet they generally assume that phenotypic readouts are measured without error. This assumption is problematic because viability-based drug response assays are inherently noisy, potentially causing models to learn experimental artefacts rather than biologically meaningful determinants of sensitivity. Here, we show that phenotypic measurement noise is present in four widely used cancer cell line screening datasets and introduce Deep Concordance Index Networks (DeepCINET), a deep learning framework that explicitly accounts for this noise. Across datasets, incorporating this noise-aware ranking strategy improves generalization across experimental conditions and to previously unseen samples. DeepCINET outperforms baseline models in multiple settings, with particularly notable gains in prioritizing the most drug-sensitive cell lines. Together, these results establish phenotypic assay noise as a critical and previously overlooked source of error in drug response modelling and provide a principled framework for noise-aware multivariable biomarker discovery.
affiliations: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University Health Network

title: Single-cell study of the FCG rat model and cross-species comparison reveal stronger gene regulation by sex chromosome complement in the medial septum
abstract: Sex differences are prominent in neuropsychiatric, neurological, and neurodegenerative conditions. While both gonads (ovaries vs. testes) and sex chromosome complement (SCC; XX vs. XY) contribute to sex differences, these effects are hard to differentiate in humans and gonadal contributions have been considered dominant in the brain. The four core genotypes (FCG) mouse model distinguishes between SCC and gonadal effects but whether findings are conserved across species remains unclear. Here, we present the first application of the novel FCG-derived rat model to explore cell-type-specific sex differences in the medial septum (MS), which shows robust structural sex differences, and convergence/divergence between species. Differential gene expression, pathway, transcription factor, and gene regulatory network analyses show dominant SCC effects and concordant gonadal effects on gene and network regulation in rat MS cell types. Comparison between the FCG rat and mouse models find convergence across species on the dominance of the SCC in regulating gene expression in concert with gonadal effects in the MS, despite divergence in individual sex-biased genes. In both species, the sex-biased, cell-type-specific MS genes and networks are associated with diverse diseases relevant to MS functions, such as anxiety, Alzheimers Disease, epilepsy, and schizophrenia, that can be targeted by proposed therapeutic candidates. Our cross-species investigation identifies a conserved dominance of SCC effects in sex-biased gene expression in the MS, thereby challenging the classical gonad-centric view of sexual differentiation in the brain and highlighting the MS as an important region for the study of sex differences driven by the sex chromosome complement.

title: PhageLysClass: Evidence-aware classification of phage lytic proteins using protein language models
abstract: Phage lytic proteins are promising antibacterial and biotechnological candidates, yet uncertain annotations, modular architectures, and class imbalance complicate sequence-based classification. We developed PhageLysClass, an evidence-aware framework for recognizing lytic proteins and distinguishing Endolysins, Depolymerases, and virion-associated lytic enzymes. From 442,329 unique phage sequences, including 11,867 evidence-supported positives, we defined distinct candidate non-target, unlabeled, and challenge populations. Seven supervised and two positive-unlabeled tasks were evaluated across factorial redundancy and train-test homology conditions, yielding 2,240 and 768 experiments, respectively. Redundancy reduction influenced generalization more strongly than homology separation, with non-additive interactions between them. ESM2-T30 consistently outperformed alternative representations and supported a hierarchical classifier achieving approximately 0.89 MCC under strict R30/S30 conditions in the selected, pre-refitting benchmark. Applied without retraining to 77,897 sequences across three collections, PhageLysClass combined predictions with physicochemical and geometric contextualization, highlighting Depolymerase-like candidates among structurally ambiguous proteins while distinguishing reference-supported assignments from extrapolation.

title: SOUR Disentangles Heritable and Microenvironmental Contributions to Intratumoral Heterogeneity in Spatial Lineage Tracing Data
abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity is hypothesized to be a major contributor to treatment resistance, yet the processes that generate it remain only partially understood. New technologies enable measurement of gene expression in individual tumor cells while also determining where the cells are located within a tumor and how they are related through cell division. A central question for such data is how much gene expression differences reflect characteristics passed from parent cells to their descendants, rather than influences from their local surroundings. Distinguishing these influences is challenging because closely related cells often reside near one another. Existing methods examine the relationship between gene expression and each of these factors separately, and can therefore incorrectly attribute spatial effects to ancestry or inherited effects to spatial location. Here, we present SOUR, a statistical method that uses both cell ancestry and spatial location to estimate their respective contributions to differences in gene expression. Using simulated data and two spatial lineage tracing datasets, we demonstrate that SOUR can estimate the separate contributions of cell ancestry and spatial location to variation in gene expression, while substantially reducing the confounding observed with existing approaches.

title: Combinatorial perturbation structure enables graded inference of signaling activity by CIRCE
abstract: Cells decode external inputs into intracellular activities of varying magnitude, and inferring both input identity and strength is crucial for cell-fate engineering. However, perturbation-response models typically treat all cells exposed to a given input as a discrete class, ignoring cell-to-cell variation in response magnitude. Here, we introduce a structured-label framework that infers both input identity and strength from combinatorial perturbation screens without dose-resolved training labels. We represent each perturbation combination in a binary combinatorial space and replace one-hot supervision with a Boltzmann distribution that decays with the Hamming distance between combinations. This approach preserves classification accuracy while improving calibration and resolving continuous pathway activities across individual cells. Importantly, intermediate scores primarily reflect ambiguity in cellular response states rather than insufficient model knowledge. Applied to engineered and natural tissues, the calibrated model successfully recovered graded activities. These results establish combinatorial perturbation screens as a self-calibrating framework for decoding graded cellular responses.
affiliations: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research / MIT

title: Sequence-Derived Geometric Priors Enable Controllable Generation of Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensembles
abstract: Predicting heterogeneous conformational ensembles from sequence remains a central challenge for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). Sequence-to-ensemble models often entangle geometric inference with coordinate generation, obscuring error sources and limiting control over ensemble properties. Here we introduce MANTA, a C-level framework that separates these stages. An encoder derives geometric priors from protein language-model representations, and a graph-Laplacian decoder converts these priors into conformational ensembles. On a homology-held-out test set, replacing predicted priors with reference-derived priors under the same decoder reduces the median absolute relative radius-of-gyration error from 8.78% to 1.89%, identifying geometric-prior estimation as the dominant bottleneck in MANTA. Across an external benchmark of 27 IDPs, MANTA generates broad, locally valid ensembles. Decoder controls modulate mean compactness and conformational breadth along partially separable axes, while compactness modulation alters motif exposure in tau and amyloid-{beta}. Meanwhile, -synuclein variants shift local exposure populations at nearly unchanged global size. MANTA provides a diagnostic and controllable framework for ensemble generation that captures both global dimensions and local conformational organization.

title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
abstract: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations. Peak lactation is characterized by expansion of luminal alveolar cells and increased {beta}-casein and -lactalbumin expression, whereas luminal progenitors, hormone-sensing cells, fibroblasts, and B cells are enriched in the dry period. Trajectory inference place luminal progenitors near branches toward alveolar and hormone-sensing states, with sustained ELF5-associated activity along the alveolar branch. Myoepithelial, macrophage, natural killer T, and T cell states are also remodeled. SPP1 and MIF signaling networks become more connected and change their cellular targets. These data establish a period resolved atlas of dairy goat mammary remodeling and identify coordinated epithelial, stromal, immune, and communication programs associated with active lactation.

title: A2Holo: Dual-Stream Flow Matching of 3D Structure and a Protein Language Model for Conformational Transition Prediction
abstract: Modelling a ligand-bound holo conformation from a ligand-free apo conformation is essential in structure-based drug discovery. We present A2Holo, which casts apo-to-holo prediction as flow matching between two experimental structures rather than generation from noise. It transplants the dual-stream joint attention of in-context image generation to residue-aligned protein language model embeddings and structure. Without ligand conditioning or stochastic sampling, A2Holo's single deterministic trajectory reaches a median C RMSD of 0.809 [A] on the D3PM benchmark, the lowest among existing methods. Its TM-score exceeds even the best of 10 samples from every stochastic baseline on at least 144 of 150 pairs. Beyond performance, we directly measure the transplanted multimodal mechanism itself. Because sequence and structure are residue-aligned, its joint attention can be measured at residue resolution and tested for reproducibility across independently trained model variants. Within the structure stream, the attention a residue receives recovers moving residues better than the attention it emits, and this asymmetry is learned. A2Holo demonstrates a successful multimodal transplant from in-context image generation to protein conformational change, with strong deterministic apo-to-holo prediction. It also provides a quantitative account of how that mechanism organises residue-aligned sequence and structure around the residues that move.

title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy.
