While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%). Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF-enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer-gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF-target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Topological centrality prioritized master transcriptional drivers governing TNBC oncogenic signaling, including CTCF, POLR2A, EP300, JUND, MYC, and FOS, which regulate Hallmark programs for Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (p = 1.2 x 10-9) and cell cycle progression. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). In silico-simulated driver feature silencing correlated with experimental responses (R2 = 0.473, p < 10-122), and master driver signatures significantly stratified overall survival in the METABRIC (n = 320) and TCGA-BRCA (n = 160; p [≤] 0.019) cohorts. Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

title: Population-level learning of non-additive effects enables accurate and efficient prediction of combinatorial perturbation responses
abstract: Combinatorial perturbations are widely used to study genetic interactions and to develop drug combinations, but the number of possible combinations grows quadratically with the number of perturbations, and only a small fraction can be measured in a screen experiment. Despite their growing sophistication, deep-learning and foundation models often fail to outperform a simple additive baseline based on measured single-perturbation responses. This suggests a simpler approach that builds on these measurements and directly learns deviations from additivity at the population level. We therefore developed GAIN, a lightweight model that implements these principles by predicting the pseudobulk response to a combination as the sum of its two single-perturbation responses and a learned interaction term. Across three single-cell datasets of genetic and drug combinations, GAIN corrected deviations from additivity and outperformed the additive model and cell-level methods across generalization settings and metrics, while training 3- to 64-fold faster. Applied to a combinatorial CRISPR screen of leukemia differentiation regulators, GAIN revealed synergy between key regulators of the differentiation block and genes that restrain differentiation but have little effect alone. It also revealed dampening by the histone chaperone FACT, which supports the induction of differentiation genes. These results establish population-level modeling of the deviation from additivity as a simple, accurate and scalable approach to predicting combination responses.
affiliations: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

title: The IGVF Catalog Knowledge Graph
abstract: The Impact of Genomic Variation on Function (IGVF) consortium is systematically characterizing how genomic variation influences regulatory elements, gene expression, and human phenotypes through thousands of experimental mapping and perturbation datasets alongside predictive models. To synthesize these diverse results into quantitative relationships and situate them within established biological knowledge, we developed the IGVF Catalog, a large-scale knowledge graph. Implemented in ArangoDB using schema-validated JSON records. Version 1.3 encompasses nearly 3 billion nodes across 14 entity types (including variants, coding variants, genomic elements, genes, transcripts, proteins, pathways, and ontology graphs for biosamples and phenotypes) connected by more than 8.6 billion edges across 31 relationship types. Edges encode statistical significance, effect sizes, source provenance, and biological context via ontology-linked hyperedges. The Catalog integrates 657 IGVF datasets spanning non-coding reporter and CRISPR perturbation screens (MPRA, STARR-seq, Perturb-seq), coding variant assays (VAMP-seq, SGE, MAVE, DUAL-IPA), and predictive models (scE2G, SEMVAR, cV2F, TLAND, and BlueSTARR), unified with extensive public context including GENCODE annotations, FAVOR and dbSNP variants, TopLD linkage disequilibrium, GWAS, QTLs, and protein interactions. Users can interrogate the Catalog through a web portal (https://igvf.catalog.org) Python and R clients, an OpenAPI-documented API featuring 86 endpoints supporting identifier and genomic-region queries, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling agent-assisted querying with large language models. We demonstrate the Catalog's utility for mechanistic interpretation across three case studies: resolving a FOXA1-dependent enhancer variant (rs11257655) regulating CAMK1D at a type 2 diabetes locus, distinguishing coding (GCKR rs1260326) and regulatory (HNF1A rs1169289) mechanisms for liver traits, and linking vascular CRISPRi-perturbed elements to CDKN2A/CDKN2B and NOS3 in coronary artery disease. Updated quarterly with open data and software, the IGVF Catalog provides a scalable resource for variant-to-function discovery.

title: Deciphering state bridges via a single-cell large language model
abstract: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed. Moreover, we successfully identified a number of well-known bridges such as bridge between Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (P = 2.21e-15), suggesting the effectiveness of the proposed framework. More importantly, we uncovered a number of new bridges. Furthermore, analyses of the number of changed cell types (NCC) and Shannon entropy revealed heterogeneous and tissue-dependent patterns of cellular composition remodeling. This study provides a new strategy for identifying disease associations and potential therapeutic relationships by deciphering bridges between biological states from scRNA-seq landscape.

title: Zero-shot virtual knock-out rankings do not recover causal genes from observational single-cell data
abstract: Background: Virtual knock-out methods rank genes by the change predicted after deleting one gene in silico and nominate targets without perturbation data. That use assumes the ranking reflects the causal consequence of removal; we tested it for three zero-shot methods in four configurations under one criterion. Results: We compared scTenifoldKnk (R and Python), CellOracle and Geneformer on 438 real, 3,585 synthetic and 330 DepMap knock-outs. Top-20 lists of different knock-outs overlapped by a median of 12 to 14 of 20, against 0.08 by chance. Displacement followed out-degree (R^2 = 0.825; 0.852 with six further features). Decoupling causal effect from topology left criterion value and grade unchanged (36 of 36 RED). For scTenifoldKnk, the ranking showed no evidence of recovery above chance where causal genes were planted (AUROC 0.538 and 0.528 in the two constructions). CellOracle's displacement showed no detectable relation to the data-built network (rho = -0.212, P = 0.556). Geneformer's shift tracked token coverage inconsistently (+0.41, +0.40, -0.27). Against DepMap essentiality, scTenifoldKnk's Python implementation (scTenifoldpy 0.5.1) reached AUROC 0.459 (95% CI 0.357-0.566), not distinguishable from chance; detection rate reached 0.588 (95% CI 0.497-0.677). Conclusions: For scTenifoldKnk and CellOracle, the ranking reports network properties, not the causal consequence of removal. No measured structural feature accounted for more than a small fraction of Geneformer's shift. Detection rate, needing no network, gained +0.129 (95% CI 0.0017-0.2543; 97.6% of resamples positive) over the tool.
affiliations: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Shanxi Provincial People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanxi Medical University, Taiyuan, 030012, Shanxi, China

title: Multi-omics causal deep learning reveals regulatory structure while interventions refine perturbation predictions
abstract: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. Here we present the Cross-Modal Causal Variational Autoencoder (CMC-VAE), which learns a network linking genes and proteins (gene-gene, protein-protein and gene-protein) in the latent space and maps each connection back onto measured features. Trained on 809,130 observational CITE-seq profiles, CMC-VAE recovers co-expression, transcription factor regulons and immune signalling programs, and learns a sparse cross-modal map enriched for transcript-protein cognate pairs. On three CRISPR screens used during development, it ranks knockout-responsive genes better than correlation and latent-VAE baselines. Fitted to a screen's unperturbed control cells, without perturbation labels, the model translates measured knockout RNA responses into protein responses better than a correlation map and cognate transcripts. The direction of gene-to-gene regulation, however, is not recovered from observational data. On the CITE-seq screens, fine-tuning only the latent network improves held-out response correlation, mainly by learning a response shared across knockouts. On larger Perturb-seq screens, with about 1,000 training perturbations, fine-tuning the latent network learns gene-specific effects that transfer to held-out genes, more so than a gene-level causal model fine-tuned on the same cells, and in simulation, such interventions also restore edge orientations that observational training leaves unresolved.

title: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation. Existing decontamination methods can struggle to distinguish intrinsic variation from contamination when both are inferred from spatial measurements alone, and may suppress genuine state-associated signals when within-cell-type heterogeneity is not explicitly modeled. Here we present Dancer, a reference-guided probabilistic framework that disentangles within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination by combining cell-type-specific gene programs learned from single-cell data with explicit modeling of intrinsic expression, neighboring-cell contamination and background RNA. Across multiple human tumor datasets with varying gene compositions and panel sizes, Dancer improves cell-type separation and expression specificity while preserving identity-associated signals, achieving superior overall performance in benchmark comparisons. Inferred gene program activities reveal within-cell-type heterogeneity in the form of distinct cellular states and continuous spatial gradients associated with local tissue environments, while reference-guided panel expansion extends molecular characterization beyond the measured genes. Together, Dancer supports accurate transcript decontamination and more faithful interpretation of cellular heterogeneity within its native tissue context.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Cell-type label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims in spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Niche analyses ask how a cell's neighbors shape its expression beyond its type. The type comes from a label, and labels are imperfect. Here we show that label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims. A mislabeled cell still expresses its true type, and because cells of a type sit near one another, the neighborhood is credited with what the label misses. Standard practice, which calls labels on the modeled counts and selects cells by them, hid, exaggerated, or reversed this inflation. Labeling one half of each cell's counts and modeling the other revealed it in nearly every population of six datasets. On semi-synthetic colon data, a labeler that over-called one fibroblast subtype reversed claims of the niche method Niche-DE; new draws of the counts and errors spread at random over subtypes almost never did. Our software, nichepeek, reports the direction of this bias in a user's data.

datasets_used: six spatial transcriptomics datasets (unnamed in abstract)
llm.novelty_zh: 首次系统指出细胞类型标签误差会在空间转录组邻域（niche）分析中系统性放大邻域效应，并可能反转结论；提出用一半计数打标签、另一半建模的诊断方法及配套软件 nichepeek。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究指出空间转录组 niche 分析中，细胞类型标签误差会因同类细胞空间聚集而被错误归因于邻域效应，从而夸大甚至逆转 niche 结论。作者通过将计数拆分为标签与建模两部分进行诊断，并在六个数据集及半合成结肠数据上验证该偏差，同时发布了用于估计偏差方向的软件 nichepeek。该工作聚焦空间组学分析的方法学偏差，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模的核心主题关系较弱。

title: ELLA-mix: Detecting Cell-to-Cell Heterogeneity in Subcellular RNA Localization
abstract: Subcellular RNA localization can differ between cells expressing the same gene, yet most analyses summarize transcript positions with a single gene-level pattern. We propose ELLA-mix, a finite mixture model for identifying cell subpopulations with distinct radial localization patterns from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data. Transcript positions are normalized relative to the cell boundary and modeled using flexible spline densities within a count-conditioned nonhomogeneous Poisson process framework. Conditioning on each cell's transcript count separates differences in localization from differences in abundance. We estimate component densities and cell memberships using an expectation-maximization algorithm and select the number of patterns using the Bayesian information criterion, restricting consideration to models with stable cell assignments and sufficiently distinct components. Simulation studies evaluated the type I error and power of the test for nonuniform localization, as well as the accuracy of selecting the number of mixture components and estimating their radial distributions. ELLA-mix correctly selected the number of components in most simulated settings. In seqFISH+ mouse fibroblasts, ELLA-mix identified distinct cell subpopulations for genes previously assigned a single localization class; genes showing such variation were enriched for endoplasmic reticulum and extracellular matrix functions. In Xenium ovarian cancer tissue, more peripheral localization patterns were associated with higher proportions of proliferating cells, particularly in S phase. These results show how modeling cell-to-cell variation can reveal localization patterns and biological associations obscured by gene-level summaries.

llm.novelty_zh: 将细胞间RNA亚细胞定位差异用有限混合模型刻画，并在给定转录本计数的条件下用非齐次泊松过程区分定位与丰度差异，以发现定位模式不同的细胞亚群。
llm.summary_zh: 该文提出ELLA-mix，一种有限混合模型，用于从基于成像的空间转录组数据中识别具有不同径向定位模式的细胞亚群，并以细胞计数条件化的非齐次泊松过程和样条密度建模转录本位置。在seqFISH+小鼠成纤维细胞和Xenium卵巢癌组织中，该方法发现了按基因汇总时被掩盖的细胞间定位异质性。该工作属于空间转录组统计分析方法，与虚拟细胞或扰动建模主题仅间接相关。

title: Differential gene expression profiling of lumbar disc degeneration in the RuDDS cohort
abstract: Lumbar disc degeneration disease (LDDD) is a major structural cause of low back pain, one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, and has no disease-modifying treatment. We performed RNA sequencing of 72 intraoperative intervertebral disc samples from the Russian disc degeneration study (RuDDS) cohort, comparing severe (Pfirrmann grades IV-V) with moderate (grade III) degeneration. We identified 731 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 347 upregulated and 384 downregulated in severely degenerated discs) in the 57 samples that passed quality control. Upregulated DEGs were enriched for extracellular matrix organisation, ossification, and TGF-beta; and Hippo signalling, whereas downregulated DEGs were enriched for immune and inflammatory processes. We identified five differentially active transcription factors, including the TGF-beta; effectors SMAD3 and SMAD4 and the osteogenic regulator DLX5. Of the five, only DLX5 was also a DEG. DEGs were enriched for LDDD-associated genes from Open Targets (odds ratio = 1.68, P = 3.37 * 10-6). Connectivity mapping against the LINCS L1000 database showed that histone deacetylase inhibitors and glucocorticoids reverse the signature of severe degeneration. Together, these results point to TGF-beta-driven fibrotic and osteogenic remodelling as the dominant transcriptional feature of severe disc degeneration, and prioritise candidate genes and compounds for functional validation.
affiliations: Institute of Cytology and Genetics, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

llm.novelty_zh: 首次对RuDDS队列中72份腰椎间盘样本做RNA-seq，比较重度与中度退变的差异基因，并通过LINCS L1000连通性图谱提出可逆转重度退变特征的化合物（HDAC抑制剂、糖皮质激素）。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究对RuDDS队列的72份术中腰椎间盘样本进行RNA测序，比较Pfirrmann IV-V级与III级退变，识别出731个差异表达基因，上调基因富集于细胞外基质重塑与TGF-beta、Hippo通路，下调基因富集于免疫炎症过程。作者还利用LINCS L1000连通性分析提示HDAC抑制剂和糖皮质激素可逆转重度退变特征，并以此筛选候选基因与化合物。该工作属于疾病转录组学分析，与虚拟细胞或扰动建模核心方向关系较弱，仅在化合物反向签名部分与药物发现相关。

title: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. This spillover is niche-dependent and can therefore confound downstream analyses that rely on niche-specific differential expression. True spillover cannot be directly quantified in experimental ST data, so existing correction methods infer contamination indirectly from transcript positions or expression structure. Here we introduce SYNDRI, a post-segmentation correction method that frames spillover detection as a supervised, gene-level classification task. We develop SYNDRI-SIM to generate labeled training data by simulating spillover between spatially mapped scRNA-seq profiles. SYNDRI uses a transformer to predict gene-level spillover probabilities conditioned on each cell's expression, identity, and local neighborhood, without requiring transcript-level coordinates or deconvolution. On held-out simulated data, SYNDRI achieves an AUPRC of 0.86, compared with 0.64 for the next-best method. Across MERFISH, CosMx, and Xenium datasets, SYNDRI achieves the highest aggregate performance across metrics of cell-type separation, reference similarity, and preservation of within-cell-type heterogeneity. In a CosMx lung cancer dataset, SYNDRI removes nearly all potentially contaminating tumor and macrophage markers from differential expression between tumor-associated and stromal fibroblasts while retaining native fibroblast markers. These results demonstrate the utility of learning from simulated spillover to improve the interpretation of spatial gene expression.

llm.novelty_zh: 将成像空间转录组的转录本溢出校正转化为基于模拟数据训练的监督式基因级分类任务，并用 transformer 结合邻域信息预测溢出概率。
llm.summary_zh: 该文针对成像式空间转录组中分割误差导致的转录本溢出问题，提出后分割校正方法 SYNDRI，并配套 SYNDRI-SIM 在空间定位的 scRNA-seq 图谱之间模拟溢出以生成带标签训练数据。在 MERFISH、CosMx 和 Xenium 数据上，SYNDRI 的综合表现优于现有方法，并能在 CosMx 肺癌数据中去除差异表达中的污染标记基因。该工作属于空间转录组数据预处理，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型的主题关联较弱。

title: A noise-corrected metric for evaluating spatial transcriptomics predicted from histology
abstract: Deep learning methods that predict spatial transcriptomics from histology offer scalable molecular profiling of clinical cohorts. However, conventional correlation metrics overstate prediction quality across whole sections by crediting models for recognizing broad tissue regions, and understate fine-scale prediction quality because sampling noise dominates sparse RNA counts. To resolve this, we introduce the reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) metric. RSC randomly splits RNA counts into two halves to separate reproducible signal from sampling noise across spatial scales and within tissue regions or cell classes. Across 12 spot-level and three single-cell methods, RSC revealed that most models capture broad tissue patterns but largely miss differences between neighboring spots or cells, which whole-section correlation overlooks. Within malignant cells, RSC distinguished methods that genuinely capture part of the cell-to-cell heterogeneity from those whose scores across all cells were inflated by cell-type composition. Guided by RSC, we designed a pairwise difference loss between neighboring spots that improved fine-scale predictions on average across 11 models. RSC thus provides a foundation for benchmarking predictions, guiding model design and determining which spatial analyses histology can support.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

llm.novelty_zh: 提出 reproducible-signal correlation（RSC）指标，通过随机二分 RNA 计数来区分可复现信号与采样噪声，从而在不同空间尺度和细胞类别内评估组织学预测空间转录组的精细尺度质量，并据此设计了相邻 spot 间的成对差异损失。
llm.summary_zh: 该文指出从组织学图像预测空间转录组的常用相关性指标会因识别大范围组织区域而高估整体预测质量，同时因稀疏计数的采样噪声而低估精细尺度预测质量。作者提出 RSC 指标，并在 12 种 spot 级和 3 种单细胞方法上评测，发现多数模型只捕捉宽泛组织模式，难以区分相邻 spot 或细胞的差异。基于 RSC 设计的相邻 spot 成对差异损失在 11 个模型上平均改善了精细尺度预测。该工作属于空间转录组预测的评测方法学，与虚拟细胞的核心主题只有间接关系。

title: Niche-FATE: niche-aware inference of cell-state transitions from spatiotemporal data
abstract: Cell-state transitions depend on intrinsic transcriptional programmes and local signals. Existing spatiotemporal mapping methods largely match cells by expression or position, not by received signals. Here we introduce Niche-FATE, an optimal transport framework integrating gene expression, spatial neighbourhoods and inferred ligand-receptor signalling to estimate transition probabilities and prioritise fate-associated signals. In simulations with changing tissue organisation, Niche-FATE improved fate inference and recovery of known fate-determining signals (mean AUPRC of 0.46 versus 0.29 for the best-performing alternative). In digit tip regeneration, Niche-FATE reduced inconsistent regenerative-to-scar transition assignments from 28% without niche information to 7%. Niche-FATE also improved developmental transition inference in mouse organogenesis. In two mouse models of Alzheimer's disease, Niche-FATE linked predicted microglial transitions to local signalling, recovered amyloid plaque associations without plaque-location input and predicted transitions from disease-associated towards homeostatic-like states. Niche-FATE enables researchers to resolve divergent cellular outcomes and investigate their associated signalling environments.
affiliations: Danish Research Institute of Translational Neuroscience (DANDRITE), Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine, Aarhus University, Aarhus, Denmark

llm.novelty_zh: 将空间邻域与推断的配体-受体信号整合进最优传输框架，用接收到的信号而非仅表达或位置来匹配细胞并估计命运转移概率。
llm.summary_zh: 本文提出 Niche-FATE，一个结合基因表达、空间邻域和推断配体-受体信号的最优传输框架，用于估计细胞状态转移概率并排序与命运相关的信号。在模拟、指间断端再生、小鼠器官发生以及两种阿尔茨海默病小鼠模型中，该方法均优于不含生态位信息的基线。该工作属于细胞命运推断与空间时序建模，与虚拟细胞的动态建模相关，但不直接涉及扰动预测。

title: Functional cooperation, adaptation and synchronization of subcellular processes in cellular neighborhoods as inferred from spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Tissue-level functions emerge from pathway activities distributed across neighboring cells. Yet analyses of spatial transcriptomics mostly focus on cell type composition or signaling through ligand-receptor pairs, leaving spatial relationships between effector processes undescribed. We inferred networks of functionally interacting subcellular processes (SCPs) that are independent of shared gene products and lie beyond sibling relationships defined in parent-child hierarchies. Using those networks for the analysis of published spatial transcriptomics datasets from human kidney biopsies, we identified functionally related SCP activities between a tissue spot and its neighbors. Identified pairs of adjacent SCPs indicate functional cooperation, e.g. basement membrane assembly and cell-matrix adhesion, functional adaption, e.g. complement synthesis and inhibition, and functional synchronization, e.g. folate cycle and cobalamin metabolism or pre-mRNA splicing and nuclear mRNA export. Two independent null models, shuffling of SCP labels within the network and shuffling of spots on the tissue slice, distinguish pairs that are functionally non-random and pairs that are additionally enriched within the immediate neighborhood, separating local from tissue-wide coordination. Our results suggest that tissue physiology reflects not only cell type composition but also functional coordination between neighboring regions.
affiliations: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

datasets_used: published spatial transcriptomics datasets from human kidney biopsies (names not given in abstract)
llm.novelty_zh: 用基于通路/亚细胞过程（SCP）的功能相互作用网络分析空间转录组，并以两种零模型区分组织内局部与全局的功能协同，而非传统的细胞类型组成或配体-受体通讯。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作从空间转录组数据中推断亚细胞过程（SCP）之间的功能相互作用网络，并将其应用于人类肾活检的已发表数据集，识别相邻组织斑点之间的功能协作、适应与同步关系。通过两种独立零模型（SCP 标签打乱与组织切片斑点打乱）区分功能非随机的过程对与在邻域内额外富集的过程对。该研究聚焦组织生理的空间功能协调，与虚拟细胞或扰动建模主题关系较弱。

title: A method to disentangle enhancer-gene interactions from latent factors in single-cell multi-omics data
abstract: Mapping regulatory elements to their target genes in the cell types relevant to disease is essential for interpreting non-coding variants identified by genome-wide association studies. Single-cell multiome data, which simultaneously measure accessible chromatin and gene expression per cell, allow such peak-gene links to be inferred within individual cell types. However, shared technical and biological variation across genes and peaks, such as cell cycle, cell quality, and inter-sample differences, creates spurious links, while including sample covariates to control for this variation inadvertently removes true genotype-driven links. To address this trade-off, we developed CREMAP (Covariance-of-Residuals-based Enhancer-gene Mapping), a statistical method that estimates shared variation as latent factors from the data and adjusts for them before testing each peak-gene pair. Using CRISPRi perturbation experiments and fine-mapped eQTLs as validation benchmarks, we demonstrate that CREMAP improves the accuracy of inferred peak-gene links compared with existing methods across two cell lines and 13 cell types from human bone marrow, brain, and kidney. In kidney proximal tubule cells, CREMAP retains eQTL-supported and allele-specific links that standard approaches miss when samples are included as covariates. Furthermore, its latent factors capture previously unrecognized global signatures, including a tubular injury program. CREMAP thus enables accurate cell-type-specific peak-gene mapping from single-cell multiome data while preserving genuine genetic regulatory effects.
affiliations: Boston Children's Hospital & Harvard Medical School

datasets_used: single-cell multiome data (human bone marrow, brain, kidney)
llm.novelty_zh: 通过从数据中估计共享技术/生物学变异的潜在因子并在检验每个 peak-gene 对之前进行校正，避免了直接加入样本协变量时误删真实基因型驱动链接的问题。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作提出 CREMAP，用于在单细胞多组学（single-cell multiome）数据中推断细胞类型特异的增强子-基因连接。方法通过残差协方差估计潜在因子并校正后再检验每个 peak-gene 对，在 CRISPRi 与 fine-mapped eQTL 基准上优于现有方法。该工作属于基因调控/非编码变异解释范畴，与虚拟细胞仅间接相关。

title: ChronoClone links temporal clonal behavior to lineage output and mutation responses
abstract: Distinct stem cell clones can yield similar lineage outputs via different developmental trajectories or dynamics and respond differently to perturbation. Here, we introduce ChronoClone, an unsupervised method that groups single-cell clones by time-resolved cell-state composition into metaclones. Benchmarked against simulated ground-truth scenarios, ChronoClone demonstrates high noise tolerance compared to existing methods. Applied to an adult mouse hematopoietic lineage-tracing dataset, ChronoClone showed that clones producing the same lineage mature at different speeds, a difference the original study did not examine. Furthermore, using WT metaclones as a baseline reference for Dnmt3a- and Npm1c-mutant sister-clones, ChronoClone uncovered hidden, clone-specific mutation responses including slowed maturation and lineage composition shifts. By connecting temporal dynamics, perturbation responses, and ancestral molecular states, ChronoClone adds temporal cell-state dynamics into clonal analysis.

llm.novelty_zh: 将时间分辨的细胞状态组成用于无监督地将单细胞克隆聚类为 metaclone，并以 WT metaclone 为参照揭示 Dnmt3a、Npm1c 突变姐妹克隆的克隆特异性响应（成熟变慢、谱系组成改变）。
llm.summary_zh: ChronoClone 是一种无监督方法，依据时间分辨的细胞状态组成把单细胞克隆分组为 metaclone，在模拟数据上表现出较高的噪声耐受性。将其应用于成年小鼠造血谱系示踪数据时，发现产生相同谱系的克隆成熟速度不同，并揭示了 Dnmt3a 与 Npm1c 突变克隆的克隆特异性响应。该工作侧重于造血干细胞克隆动力学分析，与虚拟细胞或扰动响应预测的建模目标只有间接关系。

title: XenoType: Decoding cellular identity in breast cancer histology through molecular supervision
abstract: Characterizing the cellular composition of the tumor microenvironment from histological images is fundamental to understanding cancer biology and informing treatment decisions. Deep learning has enabled automated nuclear detection and classification from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images, yet cell classifiers remain largely confined to broad morphological categories owing to a reliance on manual annotations. Recent efforts have used spatial molecular measurements to supervise histological classification, but these approaches often require separate tissue sections or produce altered H&E staining, and the resulting cell-type annotations depend on subjective choices such as marker selection and clustering parameters. Here we develop XenoType, a framework that classifies cells into seven molecularly informed categories directly from routine histology, trained using paired same-section Xenium spatial transcriptomics. Cell-type annotations are reconciled from four single-cell RNA-sequencing references, reducing dependence on marker choices. Across eight held-out breast tissue sections, XenoType outperformed commonly used CellViT++ retrained on the same molecular annotations under both four-class (macro-F1: 0.703 vs. 0.569) and seven-class (macro-F1: 0.571 vs. 0.403) taxonomies, with the largest gains for myoepithelial (F1: 0.175 to 0.572) and endothelial cells (F1: 0.395 to 0.682). Molecular measurements are required only during training; at inference, XenoType uses the H&E image alone. Model-reference agreement increased consistently with annotation confidence, and XenoType generalized to an independently profiled breast tissue section from a different spatial transcriptomics platform, supporting scalable cell-type mapping from routine histology without per-specimen molecular profiling.

datasets_used: single-cell RNA-sequencing references (four, unnamed in abstract)
llm.novelty_zh: 利用同切片配对的 Xenium 空间转录组数据作为分子监督，训练只需 H&E 图像即可推断七类细胞身份的模型，并用多份 scRNA-seq 参考对注释进行共识化以减少标记基因选择的主观性。
llm.summary_zh: 该工作提出 XenoType，利用同一切片的 Xenium 空间转录组作为训练监督，从常规 H&E 图像中将细胞分为七个分子定义的类别，推理时仅需图像。在八个乳腺组织切片上，其宏 F1 显著优于在相同分子注释上重训的 CellViT++，并能泛化到另一平台的独立切片。由于研究对象是组织学图像上的细胞类型映射，与虚拟细胞主题只有间接关系，故归为非核心、非外围圈。

title: scOnion: Cross-Modal Concordance-Aware Joint Analysis of Cells and Features in Single-Cell Multiomic Data
abstract: Single-cell multiomic assays jointly profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same cells, enabling direct analysis of cross-layer coordination. However, agreement between modalities varies across cells, and existing integration methods often emphasize shared structure, potentially averaging away cell-specific cross-modal discordance that carries biological signal. Here we present scOnion, a concordance-aware computational framework that quantifies cross-modality agreement and propagates this information into downstream analyses. Starting from paired low-rank representations obtained by spectral integration, scOnion computes per-cell concordance scores, a concordance-aware joint cell embedding, and an induced cross-modal feature embedding. The cell embedding preserves structure strongly represented in either modality, improving cell-type and state resolution, while the feature embedding scores candidate regulatory element(rE)-to-gene (rE2G) pairs. Across immune, neural, and developmental functional genomic datasets, scOnion's concordance patterns are reproducible and cell-resolved, with low-concordance cells enriched for modality-specific structure. scOnion also prioritizes candidate rE2G pairs, including distal links, with stronger support from external Hi-C contacts and fine-mapped eQTL data than the baseline linkage methods. In a B-cell fate bifurcation study, scOnion reveals remodeling of concordance and rE2G coupling during lineage commitment. scOnion embeds ~70,000 cells and computes rE2G links on CPU in 30 minutes, extends naturally to other multiomic assays such as CITE-seq, and is available as open-source software.

llm.novelty_zh: 在谱整合得到的低秩表示上引入逐细胞跨模态一致性（concordance）评分，并用其修正联合细胞嵌入与特征嵌入，从而同时用于细胞分辨率提升和rE2G增强子-基因配对打分。
llm.summary_zh: scOnion 是一个面向单细胞多组学（RNA+ATAC、CITE-seq 等）的一致性感知分析框架，量化每个细胞两种模态之间的一致程度，并将其传递到联合细胞嵌入和跨模态特征嵌入中。摘要报告其在rE2G配对预测上优于基线连锁方法（借助 Hi-C 与 fine-mapped eQTL 验证），并在 B 细胞命运分叉研究中揭示一致性与调控耦合的变化。该工作属于单细胞多组学整合与调控推断方法，与虚拟细胞主题只有间接关联。

title: GASTON-VI efficiently quantifies spatial axes and molecular gradients from multi-sample, multi-modal spatial-omics data
abstract: Many tissues exhibit an underlying spatial axis along which fundamental biological processes occur due to continuous spatial gradients of cell type and molecular state. Modern spatial-omics technologies measure molecular features (e.g. gene/protein expression) at 100,000s-1,000,000s of locations within a two-dimensional (2-D) tissue slice, with large-scale atlases profiling multiple tissue slices of the same organ type across different individuals and biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). However, existing computational methods for identifying spatial molecular gradients are limited to small spatial transcriptomics datasets (1000s of cells) of a single tissue slice, while methods for integrating multiple samples do not explicitly model spatial axes nor spatial molecular gradients along such axes. Here, we present GASTON-VI, a variational inference (VI)-based deep learning model which efficiently learns an underlying spatial axis and spatial molecular gradients along this axis from multi-sample, multi-condition spatial-omics data of any molecular modality (e.g. transcriptomics, proteomics). GASTON-VI jointly learns (1) a spatial coordinate (the "isodepth") for each individual tissue slice and (2) 1-D spatial modality functions that describe molecular gradients along the isodepth for tissues of the same biological condition, while utilizing a latent variable model to account for batch effects. Further, GASTON-VI implements a statistical test for identifying molecules with differential spatial gradients across biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased). On spatial transcriptomics and proteomics data from the intestine, tonsil, and liver, we show that GASTON-VI recovers spatial axes and molecular gradients along these axes more accurately and efficiently than existing methods. In particular, applied to large-scale spatial transcriptomics and proteomics atlases, GASTON-VI reveals differential spatial gradients of gene expression along the portal vein-central vein axis in fibrotic livers, and differential spatial gradients of protein abundance along the muscularis-lumen axis across different regions of the intestine. Software availability: GASTON-VI is available at https://github.com/chitra-lab/GASTON-VI.

llm.novelty_zh: 用变分推断深度模型同时学习每张组织切片的共享空间轴（isodepth）和沿该轴的一维分子梯度，并兼容多样本、多条件及批次效应，还提供跨条件差异空间梯度的统计检验。
llm.summary_zh: GASTON-VI 是一种基于变分推断的深度学习方法，可从多样本、多条件、多模态（转录组与蛋白组）空间组学数据中学习组织的空间轴（isodepth）及沿该轴的分子梯度，并用隐变量模型校正批次效应。论文在肠道、扁桃体和肝脏数据上表明其在空间轴与梯度恢复上优于现有方法，并在纤维化肝脏和肠道中揭示了差异空间梯度。该工作聚焦组织空间结构分析，与虚拟细胞或扰动建模的关系较间接。

title: A spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of the post-pneumonectomy lung
abstract: Perturbational spatial atlases have begun to map regenerative dynamics in a variety of tissues, yet lung remodeling has not been characterized at comparable spatial and temporal resolution. Post-pneumonectomy lung regeneration (PPLR) provides a tractable mammalian model for tissue regeneration that can be studied in situ. Here, we present a spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of PPLR in Rattus norvegicus, combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq), high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (10x Genomics Xenium), and NICHES-based spatial tissue connectomics. We observe three distinct tissue architectures at successive timepoints after pneumonectomy, each characterized by coordinated shifts in local cellular composition and intercellular signaling. At Day 3 (D3), a line of interstitial macrophages colocalizes directly beneath an intact mesothelium among active mechanotransductive and inflammatory signaling. We also observe the unexpected appearance of a transitional remodeling cellular community at D7 which appears largely absent at later timepoints, marked by fibrosis- mimetic signaling. At D14, an alveologenic architecture at distal lung tissue displays a connectivity signature consistent with active de novo growth, distinct from baseline homeostasis. Our findings establish a spatiotemporal map of multicellular architecture during regenerative lung remodeling and introduce a generalizable framework for spatial connectomic analysis to be used in perturbational tissue systems biology.

llm.novelty_zh: 在大鼠全肺切除后再生模型中，结合scRNAseq、Xenium空间转录组与NICHES空间连接组，构建了时间与空间双维度的扰动组织图谱，并提出可推广的空间细胞连接组分析框架。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究以大鼠全肺切除（pneumonectomy）为组织级扰动，结合单细胞测序、Xenium高分辨率空间转录组和NICHES空间组织连接组，描绘了术后D3、D7、D14三个时间点的肺再生多细胞结构变化。文中报告了间质巨噬细胞、D7短暂出现的纤维化样信号社区以及D14的肺泡新生结构等发现。该工作属于组织再生生物学的实验图谱，与虚拟细胞的扰动建模关系较间接，故归为外围圈。

title: Engineering dynamic interkingdom communication between synthetic organelles and mammalian systems
abstract: Engineering intracellular microbes to function as synthetic organelles, or quasiorganelles, opens new avenues for controlling mammalian cell fates and function through programmable and quantitative interkingdom communication. Here, we develop a bioluminescent reporter platform to quantify the magnitude, kinetics, persistence, and spatial distribution of transcriptional regulation in mammalian host cells directed by quasiorganelles. Using an attenuated, flavin-auxotrophic Listeria monocytogenes chassis (LINQ1) engineered to deliver synthetic transcription factors, we demonstrate approximately 100-fold activation of mammalian reporter genes, with distinct kinetics and dynamics for the tetracycline transactivator and Gal4 systems. In transgenic reporter mice, LINQ1 induced approximately 25-fold reporter activation across multiple organs, with activity persisting beyond three weeks in some animals. In mice bearing triple-negative breast tumors, LINQ1 activated intratumoral transcription and, incidentally, transiently suppressed tumor growth, although responses diminished with repeated administration. These findings establish a quantitative foundation for engineering interkingdom communication in vivo to advance a new paradigm in which programmable microbial systems function as synthetic organelles to direct mammalian cell fates and function for therapeutic benefit.

llm.novelty_zh: 利用减毒、黄素营养缺陷型 Listeria monocytogenes（LINQ1）作为"合成细胞器"向哺乳动物细胞递送合成转录因子，并以生物发光报告系统在体外、转基因小鼠和三阴性乳腺肿瘤中定量转录激活的幅度、动力学与持续性。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究构建了生物发光报告平台，用于定量细菌类"合成细胞器"（quasiorganelle）在哺乳动物宿主细胞中引导的转录调控。作者使用工程化 Listeria 底盘 LINQ1 递送 tetracycline transactivator 与 Gal4 等合成转录因子，在细胞、转基因小鼠及三阴性乳腺肿瘤模型中观察到约 100 倍（细胞）和约 25 倍（小鼠器官）的报告基因激活。该工作属于合成生物学与跨界通讯工程，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型并无直接关联。
